articles.title: Duterte trial: Prosecution keeps bribery rap, prioritizes wealth case
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution team has decided to tackle the unexplained wealth allegations against Vice President Sara Duterte next, without abandoning the bribery case it had earlier…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution team has decided to tackle the unexplained wealth allegations against Vice President Sara Duterte next, without abandoning the bribery case it had earlier contemplated.
Lead public prosecutor and Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro informed the Senate Impeachment Court of the prosecution team’s decision on Monday.

“We understand that in the order of presentation of Article II, unexplained wealth, was placed at the last presentation by the prosecution. Nevertheless, Your Honor, consistent with the compliance and manifestation filed by the prosecution on June 22, 2026, the prosecution exercises its prerogative to advance the presentation of evidence for unexplained wealth,” she told the court.

“This means, however, that we’re not waiving the presentation of evidence for bribery. The only thing that is being changed, your honor, is the order of presentation. We will be proceeding to unexplained wealth first, after which, we will end with the presentation of evidence for bribery, your honor,” she added.

Presiding Officer Francis Escudero had to clarify the position of the prosecution team, noting an earlier statement by public prosecutor and Manila Rep. Joel Chua that they might drop the bribery allegation against Duterte to speed up the proceedings.
In response, Luistro repeated that they decided to maintain both Articles II and III, pertaining to unexplained wealth and bribery allegations, respectively, against the vice president.
“Only that unexplained wealth will be advanced, and it will be followed, and we’ll end on bribery,” she added.
Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison noted Luistro’s manifestation, saying that “it’s the prerogative of the prosecution to do whatever it pleases with respect to the order of its presentation.”

The prosecution team has so far completed its presentation of evidence for Article IV, pertaining to Duterte’s alleged assassination threats against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.

It is now also about to conclude the presentation of evidence for Article I, or Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds released to the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Education, which she previously headed. /mcm

articles.title: Palace to Sara Duterte: Show evidence behind safety, trust concerns
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang has challenged Vice President Sara Duterte to provide evidence that would support her claim that she does not feel safe, referring to her remarks while she was…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang has challenged Vice President Sara Duterte to provide evidence that would support her claim that she does not feel safe, referring to her remarks while she was posting bail for her grave threats charges.
Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said on Monday that there are no records, reports, or complaints regarding supposed threats to Duterte’s life.

“Noong atin pong nakausap mismo si [Philippine National Police] General [Jose Melencio] Nartatez, at kahit naman po ang NBI [National Bureau of Investigation] Director Melvin Matibag ay nagsabi na wala po silang anumang record na sinasabing pagbabanta sa buhay ng bise presidente – wala pong record, wala pong pagsusumbong, wala pong reklamo,” Castro said at a briefing.

(When we spoke directly with [Philippine National Police] General [Jose Melencio] Nartatez, and even NBI [National Bureau of Investigation] Director Melvin Matibag said that they have no record of any threats to the life of the Vice President—there is no record, no report, and no complaint.)
She added that the government continues to provide security not only to the vice president but to all Filipinos.

“At sinisiguro naman po ng pamunuan ng PNP at ng mga ahensiya na nagbibigay ng proteksyon, lahat po, hindi lang ang bise presidente, lahat po ng mga kababayan natin ay binibigyan ng proteksyon ng pamahalaan so walang dahilan para sabihing hindi safe ang bise presidente,” she added.

(The PNP leadership and the agencies tasked with providing protection are ensuring that everyone—not just the vice president—is being protected by the government, so there is no reason to say that the vice president is not safe.)

Duterte raosed the safety concerns over the weekend before posting bail at the Quezon City Hall of Justice. Before entering the Hall of Justice, Duterte repeatedly said she did not trust the police, the courts, or even the security personnel assigned to protect her.
“I do not feel safe, I really do not feel safe. I don’t trust the court, I don’t trust the police,” she told reporters and her lawyers.

After Duterte made the remark, her brother, Rep. Paolo “Pulong” Duterte, posted on his social media account an art card featuring a photo of the Vice President with the text: “I am with VP Inday. I am a Filipino, and I don’t feel safe.”
Castro said it was understandable for the lawmaker to side with his sister but maintained that there is no evidence to support their claims.
Castro also said the public should not lose faith in the country’s justice system after Duterte expressed distrust to the court.
“Hindi po dapat mawalan ng tiwala ang taumbayan sa sistema po ng ating hustisya. At kung iyan po ang kaniyang [Duterte] nais na ipahiwatig, nasa kaniya po iyan,” Castro said.
(The public should not lose faith in our justice system. And if that is what she [Duterte] intends to imply, that is up to her.)
“At hindi po natin ini-encourage ang lahat ng mga kababayan natin na hindi maniwala sa sistema ng hustisya sa ating bansa,” she also said.
(And we do not encourage our fellow Filipinos to lose faith in the justice system in our country.) /gsg

articles.title: Church, LGU partner to champion renewable energy dev’t in Mindoro
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Churches in Mindoro and several local governments have joined forces to promote renewable energy as a more affordable and sustainable alternative to the island’s…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Churches in Mindoro and several local governments have joined forces to promote renewable energy as a more affordable and sustainable alternative to the island’s dependence on diesel-fired power.

Green energy advocates launched the REnew Mindoro Caravan on September 5, seeking to improve communities’ access to renewable energy by connecting households and institutions with solar power providers and financing institutions.
The initiative is guided by the vision of making electricity “abot-kamay at abot-kaya (accessible and affordable)” for Mindoro communities.

Oriental Mindoro’s heavy reliance on diesel has contributed to high and unreliable electricity costs, according to Gerry Arances, executive director of the Center for Energy, Ecology, and Development (CEED).
“Because of diesel dependence, Oriental Mindoro endures expensive and unreliable electricity,” Arances said.
He cited data that shows that 91.43 percent of the province’s power capacity comes from diesel, with generation rates reaching P11.47 per kilowatt-hour, compared with P5.74 per kWh for hydropower.

“We must move to renewables now,” Arances said, noting that Oriental and Occidental Mindoro have an estimated combined peak demand of 122 megawatts. Advocacy group Climate Analytics, meanwhile, has identified around 34,760 MW of renewable energy potential on the island.
Arances said Mindoro could become a model for community-centered renewable energy by tapping its renewable resources and expanding solar power in households.

The proponents also linked their demand for renewable energy to protecting the environment, particularly the Verde Island Passage (VIP), one of the country’s most ecologically significant marine areas.
Mindoro is among the provinces surrounding the VIP.
Rev. Fr. Edwin Gariguez, lead convenor of Protect Verde Island Passage (Protect VIP), said the transition away from fossil fuels is necessary to protect communities and marine ecosystems.
“This ‘Season of Creation’ stewardship of our shared home is realized by eradicating the very systems designed for profit which endanger our people and the environment,” Gariguez said.
He said the ecological damage associated with fossil fuels must end and be replaced with distributed renewable energy systems, including rooftop solar installations.
Such systems, he added, can provide electricity to communities “without compromising the sanctity and safety of our oceans.”/coa

articles.title: Japanese woman goes viral for giving birth to 7th child
articles.summary: A woman in Japan went viral and captured the public’s attention after announcing the birth of her seventh child, amid the country’s falling birth rate. Japanese writer and former political candidate…

blocks.text: A woman in Japan went viral and captured the public’s attention after announcing the birth of her seventh child, amid the country’s falling birth rate.

Japanese writer and former political candidate Kotoe Hashimoto announced on social media platform X on Aug 29 that she had given birth to her seventh child, thanking the medical staff who attended to them.
The post, which includes a photo of Hashimoto cradling her newborn, has been viewed 27 million times on X and received 10,800 likes on Facebook.
In a follow-up post later the same day, she also thanked the public for their congratulatory messages.
“I believe that now is the time for Japanese women to have children,” she said. “The rise and fall of our nation depends on the active role of women.”
Her post struck a chord among the Japanese.

“I think you’re absolutely right. I feel that the key to changing the current state of Japan, which is heading towards (demographic) collapse, is precisely the conscience of Japanese women,” Facebook user Etsugaku Kankou replied to her post.
Another user, Hideto Umegaki, said: “It’s a national treasure to give birth to seven children.”

Hashimoto, who ran as a candidate under the Party of Hope during the 2017 general election, has used her social media accounts to discuss the country’s demographic challenges and advocating for Japanese women to have more children.
She was not elected, and the conservative party, which was founded by Tokyo Governor Yuriko Koike, disbanded in October 2021.
The baby’s birth comes as Japan’s fertility rate fell to a fresh record low in 2025, extending a decade-long slide despite years of government efforts to reverse the trend.

The total fertility rate – the average number of children a woman is expected to have over her childbearing years – slipped to 1.14 from 1.15 a year earlier, according to data by the country’s Welfare Ministry.
The reading was the lowest since comparable records began in 1947.

Japan, one of the world’s oldest societies, faces mounting demographic pressures. A shrinking workforce and rising social security costs are placing strain on public finances at a time when the government is also seeking to fund higher defence spending and other growth initiatives. /dl

articles.title: Afternoon classes suspended in Laguna due to heavy rains
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — Laguna Gov. Sol Aragones suspended afternoon classes at all levels in public and private schools across the province on Monday due to heavy rains brought by the enhanced southwest…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — Laguna Gov. Sol Aragones suspended afternoon classes at all levels in public and private schools across the province on Monday due to heavy rains brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon.
Aragones announced the suspension in a Facebook post after the entire province was placed under a Yellow Heavy Rainfall Warning.

“Because of this, classes (half-day) are suspended from 1:00 p.m. onwards in all public and private schools. Alternative learning modes will be implemented,” Aragones said in her advisory written in Filipino.
“Everyone, stay safe,” she added.
Under a yellow rainfall warning, affected areas may experience 7.5 to 15 millimeters of rain within an hour, with moderate to heavy rainfall possibly continuing over the next two hours.
Flooding is also possible during the yellow warning, particularly in low-lying and flood-prone areas./coa

items: The impeachment article regarding Vice President Sara Duterte's unexplained wealth will be presented earlier than planned, following the prosecution's case on her alleged misuse of confidential funds.

The House hearings had revealed discrepancies between Duterte's significant bank transactions and her net worth declarations, with the Anti-Money Laundering Council reporting suspicious transactions totaling P6.77 billion.
The prosecution has identified 15 potential witnesses for the unexplained wealth case but will continue to pursue the bribery charges against Duterte as well.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The article of impeachment concerning Vice President Sara Duterte‘s unexplained wealth will be presented earlier than scheduled.

Lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro told the impeachment court on Monday, September 7, that Article II will be presented after the prosecution wraps up its case on Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds by September 9.
“The prosecution has the discretion to change the order, considering the availability of witnesses and other relevant considerations,” Luistro said in a subsequent press conference.
“Because of the evidence unnecessary between unexplained wealth and bribery, we find it more prudent to advance unexplained wealth and we will finish with bribery,” she added.

blocks.caption: Prosecution moves up presentation of unexplained wealth case vs Sara Duterte

blocks.text: The House impeachment hearings shone a spotlight on supposed inconsistencies between the Vice President’s large bank transactions and her net worth declarations.

The Anti-Money Laundering Council had said that according to the banks, the accounts named under VP Duterte and her husband Mans Carpio were the subject of covered transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports amounting to P6.77 billion from 2006 to 2025.
Duterte’s legal team questioned the presentation of the AMLC numbers, saying an aggregate of inflows and outflows over two decades would naturally yield a bloated number.
Despite the billions of pesos in bank transactions over the years, Duterte’s net worth averaged P42 million in 15 years, peaking at P88 million in 2024.

What’s more notable is that she made zero cash and cash declaration deposits from 2019 to 2024, and modest cash on hand and cash in bank declarations during years she was in elective office between 2007 and 2018.

blocks.caption: IN NUMBERS: What impeachment hearings unveiled about Sara Duterte’s wealth

blocks.text: The prosecution listed 15 potential witnesses for the unexplained wealth case, including Ombudsman Boying Remulla, Securities and Exchange Commission director Gerardo del Rosario, AMLC Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura, financial and forensic analysts, bank representatives, and former senator Antonio Trillanes IV, who made previous exposés against the Dutertes’ bank accounts.
Luistro said, however, that her team will not drop the bribery case against the Vice President, seeking to end the prosecution’s presentation with that article of impeachment. – Rappler.com

articles.title: [Rappler’s Best] Yes, Sara Duterte is not safe
articles.summary: But someone else is safe, for now at least, apparently so he could testify against top public officials in the flood control scandal, such as former speaker Martin Romualdez

blocks.text: While you were running weekend errands or simply making up for lost sleep on Saturday morning, September 5, the country’s Vice President showed up in a courthouse in Quezon City — with just the right amount of red on her lips, just enough volume in her hair, just enough glitter on her ears, just enough puff on her sleeves.

The grand entrance — with media, bystanders, and supporters as captive audience — followed a consistent storyline and catered to a constant base: Vice President Sara Duterte is persecuted and under siege, an uncontested truth among the keyboard warriors in the Duterteverse.

items: If you missed the spectacle, you may watch it through this link. Jairo Bolledo recounts it in this piece. Don’t fret; Jairo’s video report provides context and lays out what comes after.
To those wondering whether one can post bail on a Saturday, yes you can. There’s a weekend court assigned to each regional trial court for bail proceedings, according to Jairo.

“I’m not safe,” Duterte said repeatedly before the cameras. This is like a meme version of her usual defense: that she made the remark about hiring an assassin to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former speaker Martin Romualdez because there was a supposed security threat against her.

In truth, she has an enviable armor of physical security. The Vice President’s security group remains intact, though now less than the record-number, battalion-size force that she enjoyed in her early years in the post. The Philippine National Police still teems with Duterte loyalists. Civilian and military security personnel in the Davao Region are her extended security apparatus as well.

blocks.text: But, yes, she is not safe from the bullets of accusations against her that range from abusing power to misusing taxpayers’ money to fattening her bank accounts.

items: The vice president is not immune from a court suit. Marites Dañguilan Vitug tackled this in 2015, at the height of the exposés against then-vice president Jejomar Binay. Constitutionalists have pointed out that it’s only the president who’s immune from suit while in office. Read more.

The criminal charges Duterte is facing before a Quezon City regional trial court make her the first vice president to be charged in a regional trial court in recent history. Binay was charged in court, but in the anti-graft Sandiganbayan, over a graft case that was downgraded from plunder. He was acquitted in 2025.

Former president Gloria Macapagal Arroyo was also charged in a lower court (in Pasay) under the Noynoy Aquino administration, but this was over an election fraud case. Arroyo was arrested in November 2011 and put under hospital detention until she was granted bail. Read more.

blocks.text: The case against Vice President Duterte in a Quezon City court is not only bailable but defensible in that she has the luxury of time and multi-level appeals to make this go away.

items: The impeachment trial is another matter altogether; her threats against the Marcoses are in the fourth article of impeachment and the first to be presented by the prosecution last July.

As the prosecution prepares to present the complaint about Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth in the third week of September, the possibility of a plunder suit against her looms. All public officials previously charged with plunder were jailed immediately.

A conviction by the Senate impeachment court disqualifies Duterte from public office. Granted she’s acquitted, will the 2028 presidential race be a walk in the park for her? She is the clear front-runner in surveys for the 2028 presidential elections, but data shows that four out of five presidential polls saw early survey leaders fall from grace. Check this data story.

blocks.text: But someone else is safe, for now at least, apparently so he could testify against top public officials in the flood control scandal, such as former speaker and presidential cousin Martin Romualdez — the “central figure” in the scandal.

items: Former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan, under whose term massive ghost and graft-ridden corrupt flood control contracts were deployed, was released on September 3, following the Sandiganbayan’s swift dismissal of plunder and graft charges filed by the Ombudsman against him with the 5th Division. A separate graft case against him is still pending in the 2nd Division.

It was only three months ago when Ombudsman Boying Remulla announced that his office had reached a deal with Bonoan for him to turn state witness to strengthen government’s cases against those involved in flood control corruption.
In particular, the Ombudsman said it was eyeing Bonoan to pin down Romualdez in the plunder, money laundering, and graft cases being built against him.

An appointee of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Bonoan is a province mate of the President in Ilocos Norte. When he was public works secretary, his department awarded P2.5 billion worth of projects to his daughter’s business partner. He was forced to quit in August 2025.
Asked for updates at a budget hearing on September 3, Ombudsman Remulla said there are now 35 flood control-related cases pending in courts, 31 of which are with the Sandiganbayan.

articles.title: Prosecution to advance presentation of evidence on Sara Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel on Monday said they will present in advance Article 2 of the impeachment case, which refers to the alleged unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 3:44pm
The House prosecution panel on Monday said they will present in advance Article 2 of the impeachment case, which refers to the alleged unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte.
House lead prosecutor and Batangas Representative Gerville Luistro said this on the 22nd day of the impeachment trial.

“We understand that in the order of presentation of articles, Article 2, unexplained wealth was placed at the last presentation by the prosecution. Nevertheless, Your Honor, consistent with the compliance and manifestation filed by the prosecution on June 22, 2026, the prosecution exercises its prerogative to advance the presentation of evidence for unexplained wealth,” Luistro said.
She, however, emphasized that the prosecution is not waiving the presentation of evidence for the bribery charge under Article 3 of the impeachment case.

“The only thing that’s been changed, Your Honor, is the order of presentation. We will be proceeding to the unexplained wealth first. After which, we will end with the presentation of evidence for bribery,” Luistro said.
She also clarified that “as of this moment,” the prosecution has decided to maintain both the Articles 2 and 3 in the presentation of evidence.

This came after House prosecution spokesperson Joel Chua said last week that they are considering dropping the bribery charge, as the prosecution wants to focus on what it considers its strongest allegations.
Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison took note of Luistro's manifestation, saying that it is the prerogative of the prosecution to “do whatever it pleases with respect to the order of its presentation.”

Article 2 alleged that Duterte amassed unexplained wealth manifestly disproportionate to her lawful income and earnings during her incumbency as a public official; failed to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN); and failed to divest, and instead, willfully continued, all her business interests during her tenure as Vice President.

Meanwhile, Article 3 alleged that the Vice President must be impeached for committing bribery by giving monetary gifts or payments to Department of Education (DepEd) officials to induce the violation and circumvention of procurement and other related laws. — RSJ, GMA News

On Sunday night, Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD’s lead candidate, thanked Musk on X…

blocks.text: Morning opening: What now after AfD's election triumph?

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa

Europe wakes up this morning to final results of the Saxony-Anhalt state election in Germany, with the far-right Alternative für Deutschland confirmed as the winners – but without a majority in the state parliament.

blocks.caption: AfD leaders Ulrich Siegmund, Tino Chrupalla, and Alice Weidel, on stage at AfD election party for the 2026 state election under a slogan “It begins here.” Photograph: dts News Agency Germany/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Cue chaotic discussions about what’s next, including theoretical scenarios with defections, a minority government backed on issue-by-issue basis by the far-left Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance, or even… a snap election to resolve the deadlock.

We are expecting to hear from the embattled German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, around lunchtime. With German media running grainy pictures of Merz looking glumly on the backseat of his car, it is probably fair to say that the pressure on him will only increase.
There are also lots of political reactions from across Europe, with no doubt more to come.
I will bring you all the latest here.
Separately, I will keep an eye on Ursula von der Leyen’s trip to Greenland amid renewed US interest in the territory, and on the funeral of Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladić.
It’s Friday, 4 September 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.
Key events

items: 3m agoEuropean leaders concerned about AfD win
10m agoRussian presidential aide praises 'historic' win for 'pragmatic' pro-Russian AfD
16m agoAfD state leader thanks Elon Musk for support after Saxony-Anhalt win

blocks.text: European leaders concerned about AfD win
We are also getting first reactions from European ministers.
Donald Tusk, the prime minister of Poland, said:
“In Poland, only idiots or traitors can rejoice at the triumph of the AfD in Germany.”
Poland’s foreign minister Radosław Sikorski called the AfD’s win “a very worrying” signal for Europe.
France’s Europe minister, Benjamin Haddad, described the win as “a serious moment in Europe”, warning that “nationalism and xenophobia will never be a solution”.
“We must listen with humility to the anger, the concerns, the fears, and respond to them,” he added. “We cannot forget our history. That is the meaning behind the choices made by France and Germany.”
French finance minister Roland Lescure joined in his warnings, saying Europe faced “a major challenge in the face of a populist wave” across the continent.
But former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán celebrated AfD’s win, saying it was “a huge night for Germany and Europe!”
“Buckle up. This is just the beginning!”
Russian presidential aide praises 'historic' win for 'pragmatic' pro-Russian AfD
Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev took a screen grab of US president Donald Trump’s post on Saxony-Anhalt and praised a “historic win for the pragmatic AfD”.
AfD is pro-Kremlin, urging a stop to support for Ukraine and pushing for Ukrainians to no longer receive refugee status.
AfD state leader thanks Elon Musk for support after Saxony-Anhalt win

On Sunday night, Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD’s lead candidate, thanked Musk on X “for your support and for your clear and highly important perspective on the political developments of our time”, adding: “I would very much welcome the opportunity for strong and constructive cooperation”.

blocks.caption: Alice Weidel, co-leader of the Alternative for Germany party (AfD), speaks as SpaceX CEO Elon Musk appears on screen during a central election campaign event of the AfD in Halle (Saale), Germany in January last year. Photograph: Karina Hessland/Reuters

blocks.text: Siegmund wrote his comments after Musk said “Well done!” in German to AfD co-founder Alice Weidel, when she posted about the projected win.

articles.title: Remulla on plunder case vs. Martin Romualdez: He is big fish
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said Monday that government prosecutors filed a case against a big fish, with plunder charges against Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez and three others.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 3:36pm
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said Monday that government prosecutors filed a case against a big fish, with plunder charges against Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez and three others.
“Sa ngayon [siya ang big fish]. At hindi pa naman ito ‘yung huling kaso eh. Sunod-sunod pa ito. At marami pa kaming pa-file-an. Ibang-iba ito,” Remulla said in a press conference.
(He is the big fish for now. This is not the end of cases for him. There will be more, and we will be filing cases against more people. Different cases.)

Ombudsman prosecutors alleged that Romualdez accumulated P7.4 billion worth of kickbacks off government projects from 2022 to 2025 "from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects funded under the General Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2022 to 2025, which monies were delivered to properties owned by, occupied by, or associated with Romualdez and received by [co-accused Joselyn Tragua] Serenio and other persons acting for and in his behalf."

“Kasi alam naman natin, hindi iba si Martin Romaldez sa akin o sa Presidente o kahit kanino man. Ngunit ito, ito ‘yung aming obligasyon sa bayan na gawin ang tama. Ito lang ang pinatutupad natin dito. Wala ho itong sinisino,” Remulla added.
(Martin is no stranger to me, the President, or anybody. But it is our obligation to do what is just. That is what we are doing here. There are no sacred cows.)
Romualdez is a former colleague of Remulla in the House of Representatives and cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr.

Likewise, Remulla assured the public that the filing of the plunder case against Romualdez, former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list , as well as two others are based on strong evidence.

“Wala po itong ginagalang o kaya iniiwasan na pangalanan. Lahat po ito ay base sa ebidensya. Iyon ang mahalaga rito eh. Itong kasong to, talagang nagpapatunay na hindi po kami kumikiling kahit kanino,” he said.
(We are not shying away from anybody. These are all grounded on evidence. This case will prove that we are not protecting anybody.)
“Ang gusto lang namin dito, managot ang dapat managot (What we are after here is accountability),” Remulla added. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: DepEd seeks P10B more for laptops as proposed 2027 budget funds only 50,000
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) is seeking an additional P10 billion for laptops after the proposed 2027 budget provided funding for only 50,000 units, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said…

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 3:33pm

The Department of Education (DepEd) is seeking an additional P10 billion for laptops after the proposed 2027 budget provided funding for only 50,000 units, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said Monday.

Angara made the statement during the House Committee on Appropriations hearing on DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget, after Representative Edgar Erice asked about the administration’s promise to provide laptops to public school teachers.
Angara said DepEd is distributing 283,000 laptops this year, which he described as the biggest single allocation for teachers in any year.

“Well, this year we’re giving, I think, over 200,000 laptops, 283,000 laptops, which again is not business as usual, Your Honor. We have about 870,000 teachers. This is the biggest single allocation in any year for our teachers,” Angara told the House committee on appropriations.
He said the distribution would cover nearly one-third of DepEd’s roughly 870,000 teachers.
Erice then asked whether DepEd could eventually provide laptops to all public school teachers by the end of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s term.
Angara said the proposed 2027 budget has funding for only 50,000 laptops, prompting the department to seek additional funds.
“Sa 2027 budget, there’s funding only for 50,000 laptops, Your Honor. That’s why we’re requesting an additional 10 billion para fulfill po yung pangako niya,” he said.
(In the 2027 budget, there’s funding only for 50,000 laptops, Your Honor. That’s why we’re requesting an additional 10 billion to fulfill his promise.)
The laptop request is part of DepEd’s broader appeal for additional funding for programs not accommodated under the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP).
DepEd is seeking P145.19 billion in additional funding on top of its proposed NEP allocation to address funding gaps for learning recovery, personnel hiring, school safety and other programs.
The department said the supplemental request includes funding for teacher benefits, training, laptops and other support mechanisms intended to allow teachers to focus on teaching.
'Sustained' laptop rollout
Angara earlier acknowledged the challenge of sustaining the laptop distribution, noting that providing 283,000 units in one year would cover nearly one-third of the teaching workforce.
“So again, the question is sustainability. Dahil kung hindi natin ma-sustain ito, hindi natin mabibigyan lahat,” he said.
(So again, the question is sustainability. Because if we cannot sustain this, we cannot provide them to everyone.)
He said the current year’s rollout represented a significant departure from the usual level of support for teachers.
Erice had asked whether the President’s promise could ultimately result in every public school teacher receiving a laptop before the end of his term.

DepEd presented a proposed P975.96-billion budget for fiscal year 2027, including allocations for its attached agencies, before the House Committee on Appropriations, according to the department’s press release.
The department is seeking an additional P145.19 billion for critical programs not funded under the 2027 NEP.

Under the proposed NEP allocation, Personnel Services would rise 8.64% to P766.74 billion, while Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) would decline 15.94% to P174.32 billion and Capital Outlay would fall 67.49% to P32.34 billion.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: India news: Rescue efforts underway in deadly Delhi building collapse
articles.summary: The building was located in New Delhi's Satya Niketan, popular among students from nearby colleges and universities. At least 12 people have been rescued from the rubble. DW has more.

image.caption: The incident took place close to Delhi University's South Campus, in an area popular with studentsImage: Francis Mascarenhas/REUTERS

blocks.text: The building was located in New Delhi's Satya Niketan, popular among students from nearby colleges and universities. At least 12 people have been rescued from the rubble. DW has more.

blocks.caption: The incident took place close to Delhi University's South Campus, in an area popular with studentsImage: Francis Mascarenhas/REUTERS

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: At least seven people have died after a building collapsed in Delhi
The building was located in South Delhi's Satya Niketan, popular among Delhi University students
Rescue operations are underway

blocks.text: Below is a roundup of the top headlines from India on Monday, September 7.

September 7, 2026
At least 7 people killed as rescue efforts continue

blocks.caption: Officials said water accumulated at the base of the buildingImage: Francis Mascarenhas/REUTERS

blocks.text: The death toll has risen to seven after rescue personnel recovered another body amid the rubble of a five-story building in India's capital city Monday, a day after the nearly 50-year-old structure came crashing down.

The building was located in Satya Niketan, a popular student hub that houses hundreds of university students often living in crowded conditions. It is situated in close proximity to Delhi University's South Campus, making it a popular destination for students.
Local media reported that the building housed a private hostel.
In its latest update, Delhi Police said a total of 12 people had been rescued during the operation. Emergency crews say more people may be trapped in the rubble.
Rescue teams, including personnel from disaster agencies as well as fire and police teams, were using heavy machinery and sniffer dogs to locate those trapped.

blocks.caption: The exact moment that the building collapsed was caught on CCTVImage: Vipin/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Earlier, the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), which is treating victims of the collapse, said its trauma center received 10 people: "Out of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while one patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to his injuries."

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta addressed the potential cause of the collapse, saying: "It is certain that there was ‌water in the building's basement, and due ‌to ​accumulation of water, due to ongoing repair work, the old building collapsed."

The police have registered a First Information Report (FIR) under Sections 105, 290 and 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (the official criminal code of India) against the building owners, local media reported. The specific sections relate to culpable homicide, negligence in the construction or repair of buildings as well as acts that endanger human life.

articles.title: Duterte trial: Prosecution withdraws ex-DepEd SDO Fajarda as witness
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution panel in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial has withdrawn former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda as a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution panel in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial has withdrawn former Department of Education (DepEd) special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda as a witness as he recovers from a stroke.

Fajarda was supposed to testify in late August regarding Article I, or the alleged misuse of confidential funds (CF) within DepEd when Duterte still headed it. However, this was postponed after he suffered a stroke.
The House prosecution panel then made Fajarda a reserved witness after his physician initially recommended two weeks of rest.
However, Fajarda’s legal counsel submitted to the Senate Impeachment Court on Monday morning that he would need another month to recover.

“In view of the latest medical update, and the confirmation by the doctors of the Senate, as a humanitarian consideration, we are going to dispense with the testimony of the witness, and we wish him well,” private prosecutor Reynaldo Robles said during Duterte’s trial on Monday.
The House prosecution opted to recall Fajarda’s subpoena to appear before the court and instead pursued stipulations.

The defense earlier stipulated that Duterte’s security officer, Col. Dennis Nolasco, received the DepEd P112.5 million in confidential funds from Fajarda, following Duterte’s orders when she was education secretary from 2022 to 2024. /mcm

articles.title: SC: 463 judge positions still vacant, causing case backlogs
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A total of 463 judge positions remain vacant, which contribute to the continuous backlogs of cases in courts across the country, the Supreme Court (SC) told the House of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A total of 463 judge positions remain vacant, which contribute to the continuous backlogs of cases in courts across the country, the Supreme Court (SC) told the House of Representatives on Monday.

SC Administrator Theresa Dolores Gomez-Estoesta said this during the House committee on appropriations’ hearing on the proposed 2027 budget for the judiciary, after Kabataan party-list Rep. Renee Co raised concerns about the lack of judges in the country despite the recent creation of new regional trial courts and family courts.
“Ang judge vacancies po namin as of now, 463 po. It represents 16.7 percent of the authorized judicial positions,” Gomez-Estoesta said.
(Our judge vacancies as of now are 463. It represents 16.7 percent of the authorized judicial positions.)
According to Gomez-Estoesta, some courts in the country remain “unorganized” because a Notice of Staffing and Classification Action (NOSCA) has not yet been issued.
She explained that NOSCA is a document issued by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) to authorize the creation of a judge or court personnel position.
“If there is no NOSCA yet issued, we call it the unorganized courts. And despite the fact that we want to fill them in, we cannot do so because of the lack of a NOSCA,” the SC administrator said.

“Dahil unfilled po yung 463, kailangan po talaga na antayan namin ang NOSCA, but hopefully this will be remedied by the Fiscal Autonomy Act because the DBM po ay nabibigyan lang po siya ng 120 days para i-issue po siya. Otherwise, the Supreme Court will now resort to other appropriate measures just to have it funded with the DBM,” she explained.

(Since the 463 is unfilled, we really need to wait for the NOSCA, but hopefully this will be remedied by the Fiscal Autonomy Act because the DBM is only given 120 days to issue it. Otherwise, the Supreme Court will now resort to other appropriate measures just to have it funded with the DBM.)

After hearing this, appropriations committee vice chairperson and Cagayan de Oro Rep. Rufus Rodriguez interjected, urging the SC to finish promulgating the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) for the Judiciary Fiscal Autonomy Act that could open judge positions.

“Promulgate the IRR for the law so that we can already open them because some courts, five to seven years nang na-create. There is a felt need in many districts, cities, and provinces for courts to already be organized. Grabe na rin ang backlogs eh (The backlogs are too bad.),” he said.
Responding to this, SC Associate Justice Jose Midas Marquez said the IRR has already been submitted to the Court En Banc and is under review.
The associate justice mentioned that the court is only on recess this September, noting that come October, “we will push for its approval already.”
Marquez, meanwhile, explained that some of the provisions of the law are “self-implementing.”

“So kahit hindi po natin antayin yung IRR, pwede na po natin gampanan yung ating mandato na maging fiscally autonomous ang judiciary. So we can already proceed with the filling up of these courts and maibigay sa JBC (Judicial and Bar Council) para mabuksan na po yung position for application for judges, and thereafter lalagyan na po natin ng mga court personnel,” the associate justice said.

(So, even without waiting for the IRR, we can already fulfill our mandate for the judiciary to be fiscally autonomous. We can proceed with staffing these courts and refer the matter to the JBC (Judicial and Bar Council) so that applications for judgeships can be opened, after which we will fill the court personnel positions.)

When asked if the budget for the filling up of positions is already included in the 2027 proposed budget, the SC administrator said, “The appropriations will come from the DBM,” citing the need for the NOSCA.
Rodriguez then asked the DBM’s side about this matter.
In response, DBM Director Carlos Castro said the judiciary currently has only three pending budget requests related to the creation of positions.

“Nevertheless, kapag ito ay nafill-up-an ng judiciary, meron naman po tayong mapagkukunan ng pondo, meron po tayong miscellanious personnel benefits fund. Ni-rerelease din naman po natin ito upon the release of the judiciary,” the DBM official said.
(Nevertheless, when this is filled up by the judiciary, we have a source of funding; we have a miscellaneous personnel benefits fund. We also rereleased it upon the release of the judiciary.)
The judiciary is seeking an P86.27 billion budget for 2027, around 22 percent more than its P70.61 billion budget in 2026. /gsg

articles.title: Manila leptospirosis cases reach ‘epidemic’ levels – health officer
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The local government of Manila is now considering the leptospirosis situation in the city an “epidemic” due to a rise in reported cases, the city’s health officer…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The local government of Manila is now considering the leptospirosis situation in the city an “epidemic” due to a rise in reported cases, the city’s health officer said on Monday.

A statement from the Manila Public Information Office showed that the city’s health office observed that leptospirosis cases had already surpassed the city’s “epidemiologic threshold,” as incidence rose to 3.48% from 1.27% the previous week, indicating a rapid increase in cases over a short period.
This prompted Manila OIC-City Health Officer Dr. Grace Padilla to state that the spread of leptospirosis is already in an “epidemic condition.”

She reported that several city government district hospitals, including Ospital ng Maynila, Sta. Ana Hospital, and Justice Jose Abad Santos General Hospital, had reached full capacity because of the increase in patients.

Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso directed local government agencies to intensify their campaign against leptospirosis, including an aggressive public information campaign to inform residents that free doxycycline capsules are available at all 44 health centers and seven district hospitals operated by the city government.

Domagoso said it would be better for the city government, through the Manila Health Department and the 896 barangays, “to go directly to residents and distribute doxycycline to those affected by flooding in recent weeks.” /mcm

articles.title: Crowds gather for war criminal Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade
articles.summary: BELGRADE — Crowds began gathering in Belgrade on Monday morning for the funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, as Brussels accused some in the country of “glorification” of…

blocks.text: BELGRADE — Crowds began gathering in Belgrade on Monday morning for the funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, as Brussels accused some in the country of “glorification” of a man convicted of genocide during the 1990s war in Bosnia.
Mladic died in late August, aged 84, while serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the war in Bosnia.
Mourners streamed into St Luka church in Belgrade from 7am (0500 GMT) to pay respects, with many kissing Mladic’s closed coffin, as Serbian Orthodox priests read prayers.
Police had closed off streets in the surrounding part of the city as crowds began arriving.
AFP reporters saw large crowds outside the church, many wearing shirts praising Mladic, as doors opened with aerial images showing hundreds already queuing to enter.
Serbian flags had been hung nearby, and a huge banner unfurled across the street read: “Welcome, General, thanks be to your mother for bearing a hero, so that Serbdom’s glory may return.”
“I am here to see off the general, a national hero,” pensioner Radojka Visic, who had travelled from Bosnia’s Serb entity, Republika Srpska, told AFP.
“They couldn’t defeat us on the battlefield, so they sent him to prison and tortured him there instead,” Visic said, referring to the “international community”.
Backlash
Mladic’s casket arrived in the country last week aboard a government plane, where it had been carried by six soldiers and draped in flags.
As it was driven from the airport in a motorcade, groups of young men held banners praising the former general, and some police were seen saluting as it passed.

Last week’s scenes drew condemnation from the European Union’s enlargement commissioner, Marta Kos, who cancelled a forthcoming visit to Serbia on Friday, saying the “glorification surrounding his death is incompatible with the values on which the EU path is built”.
Denis Becirovic, chairman of Bosnia’s tripartite presidency, called it “an act of identification by Serbia’s leadership with one of the worst killers in European history”.
“This has unforeseeable consequences for the future of the entire region,” he wrote on Facebook on Friday.
Mladic’s wartime atrocities during the break-up of the former Yugoslavia earned him the nickname “Butcher of Bosnia” in international media.
The 1992-1995 war left around 100,000 people dead and displaced 2.2 million.
Mladic was the military figurehead of the Bosnian Serb leadership alongside former Yugoslav president Slobodan Milosevic and Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic.
The United Nations war crimes court convicted him of genocide over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, where Bosnian Serb forces killed around 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys in a UN-protected safe zone.
The atrocity was Europe’s worst act of bloodshed since World War II.
Fadila Efendic, whose son and husband were killed in Srebrenica, told AFP earlier that it pained her “to know that his ideas are not dead”.

Mladic was also convicted of persecuting and forcibly expelling Bosnian Muslims and Croats, terrorising civilians during the siege of Sarajevo and taking UN peacekeepers hostage during NATO air strikes in 1995.
‘Hero’
Mladic was arrested in 2011, 16 years after he was first indicted, and sentenced to life in prison in 2021 after a nine-year trial.
Despite the verdicts, he is still hailed as a hero by some Serbs, particularly in Republika Srpska, where his death was marked with vigils and gatherings.
Many from the entity have applied to travel to Belgrade for the funeral.
Mladic’s son Darko, who is officially organising the funeral, said he was “proud of the role” his father played.
On Saturday, around 300 people gathered at a commemoration for Mladic at a military facility in Belgrade, organised by an association of retired and active Serbian army generals.
Darko and other family members also attended, as well as Serbian Justice Minister Nenad Vujic and officials from Republika Srpska, including President Sinisa Karan.
Speakers at the ceremony praised Mladic’s wartime role, describing him as a “towering figure both as a man and a soldier”.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic said that tens of thousands of people were expected to attend the funeral and that the state would ensure the event passed “safely”.
He would not attend in person due to a prior engagement, he explained. /dl

articles.title: Calabarzon police seize P13.3M worth of illegal drugs in a week
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — Police in the provinces of Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal and Quezon seized more than P13.3 million worth of illegal drugs during anti-narcotics operations conducted across Calabarzon…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — Police in the provinces of Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal and Quezon seized more than P13.3 million worth of illegal drugs during anti-narcotics operations conducted across Calabarzon from Aug. 31 to Sept. 6.
The Calabarzon police reported on Monday (Sept. 7) that 228 suspects were arrested in 181 drug busts last week.

Police seized 1,922 grams of shabu (crystal methamphetamine), 1,973.97 grams of marijuana, and 61.72 grams of high-grade marijuana, locally known as “kush,” with a combined estimated value of P13,399,056, the report said.
Highlighted by the report was the seizure of P8,160,000 worth of shabu from two high-value drug suspects in Batangas City on Sept. 1 and 2.
During the whole month of August, police arrested 1,156 suspected drug traffickers and confiscated illegal drugs worth P19,772,573 in various operations across Calabarzon.
The value of drugs seized in August was lower than the P29.5 million worth confiscated by police in July.
The suspects were detained and faced complaints for alleged violations of Republic Act No. 9165./coa

articles.title: Recto says proposed P300-M allotment to complete Bukidnon airport
articles.summary: QUEZON, Bukidnon — Executive Secretary Ralph Recto announced a proposed P300 million allocation under the 2027 national budget to finally complete the long-awaited Bukidnon Airport in the…

blocks.text: QUEZON, Bukidnon — Executive Secretary Ralph Recto announced a proposed P300 million allocation under the 2027 national budget to finally complete the long-awaited Bukidnon Airport in the municipality of Don Carlos.

Recto announced this during his visit here last Friday, September 4, where he also led the distribution of rice aid and Local Government Support Funds (LGSF), and awarded P20,000 each to 155 college students from the town’s 31 barangays as presidential scholars under the Socio-Civic Projects Fund (SCPF).
Following his engagement in Quezon, Recto personally inspected the ongoing construction of the airport facility.

He emphasized that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has issued a strict directive to finish the project without delay, ensuring it will not be left idle.The fresh P300 million funding brings the Marcos administration’s total financial commitment to the project to P1.36 billion, pushing the overall government investment in the airport to P3.17 billion.Designed to accommodate commercial jet aircraft such as the Airbus A320, the strategic transport hub features a 2,100-meter runway, a six-aircraft apron, and a modern passenger terminal that can serve up to 425 passengers at a time.National and local leaders underscored that once operational, the facility will directly link Bukidnon to major tourism and business centers nationwide.Officials noted it will significantly accelerate the transport of prime agricultural products—including pineapples, bananas, corn, coffee, sugar, and livestock—to larger markets while driving regional investments and creating local employment opportunities./coa

articles.title: Man given 6 months to live; spends it finding home for autistic son
articles.summary: SINGAPORE — Jeon Gyeong-cheol, the author widely known as the “Peter Pan Dad” for documenting his search for a home where his disabled son could live after his death, died Saturday.…

blocks.text: SINGAPORE — Jeon Gyeong-cheol, the author widely known as the “Peter Pan Dad” for documenting his search for a home where his disabled son could live after his death, died Saturday. He was 64 and had been fighting late-stage liver cancer.

Jeong Yu-jin, head of the Developmental Disabilities Support Expert Forum, announced Jeon’s death on social media Sunday, saying the funeral would be held without a formal wake, in accordance with his wishes.
“He is currently at the hospital, and no separate memorial hall will be set up. We extend our deepest condolences,” she wrote.
Jeon spent more than two decades as the sole caregiver for his son, who is now 27 and has autism, with his developmental level assessed as that of a 2- or 3-year-old.

After receiving a terminal diagnosis of late-stage liver cancer in April last year, Jeon traveled across the country, reaching out to nearly 1,000 care facilities in hopes of finding a place that could look after his son once he was gone. Few, however, were able to take him in.

Jeon later began writing about his search on the content publishing platform Brunch, and his accounts struck a chord with many readers. His story soon reached a wider audience through television programs including MBC’s “True Story Expedition” and tvN’s “You Quiz on the Block.”
Jeon later compiled his writings on Brunch into the essay collection “Annyeong, Peter Pan,” published in June.

Readers moved by his story raised some 80 million won ($59,000) in donations, and with growing nationwide support, Je-won was able to move into a community village for people with profound developmental disabilities.

“I want to tell him to forget about his dad and live happily. But I don’t want him to forget me completely. I hope he remembers me with a faint sense of longing, as an old man who once looked at him with warmth,” Jeon said on “You Quiz on the Block” last month.
Jeon also sought to help families facing struggles similar to his own, working to establish a welfare foundation for adults with severe autism-related disabilities, like his son.

On Aug. 26, shortly before his death, he announced the launch of a preparatory committee for the foundation. With the committee now in place, its members are expected to carry on Jeon’s efforts and continue discussions on launching the foundation, according to news reports. /dl

articles.title: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanese village kill 11, state media say
articles.summary: Lebanon says renewed attacks jeopardise a US-brokered ceasefire meant to end the conflict between Israel and armed group Hezbollah.

blocks.text: Israeli air strikes on a village in southern Lebanon have killed at least 11 people, including two children, Lebanese state media say.

Nine people were killed in one strike that destroyed a three-storey residential building in Kfar Rumman shortly after midnight, while two paramedics were killed in a second strike on a car, according to the National News Agency.
The Israeli military said it was looking into the reports.

On Sunday, Israeli strikes killed seven people in southern Lebanon, as the Israeli military retaliated for what it said were drone attacks by the armed group Hezbollah on its troops in occupied areas of the country.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks were a "dangerous escalation" that jeopardised the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in June, which was meant to end the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

articles.title: Palace on Martin Romualdez plunder case: Those accountable must face charges
articles.summary: Malacañang on Monday said anyone who is found to be accountable for wrongdoing should face the consequences, regardless of political affiliation or personal ties to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 3:23pm
Palace on Martin Romualdez plunder case: Those accountable must face charges
Malacañang on Monday said anyone who is found to be accountable for wrongdoing should face the consequences, regardless of political affiliation or personal ties to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro made the statement after the Office of the Ombudsman filed a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
Romualdez is a cousin of Marcos.

“Sa Pangulo naman po ay kung sino po ang dapat na managot ay dapat na panagutin. Kung sino man po ‘yan– kamag-anak, kaibigan, kaalyado, o kalaban sa pulitika– kung ano po ang isinisigaw ng ebidensya, dapat lamang po itong mailahad,” she said at a press briefing.

(As for the President, whoever should be held accountable must be held accountable. Whoever they are– relatives, friends, allies, or political opponents– whatever the evidence reveals, it should be presented.)
“So, depende na po yan sa mga makakasuhan kung sila naman po ay may sapat na ebidensya para ipaglaban ang kanilang sarili, nasa kanila na po iyan,” she added.
(So, it depends on those who will be charged whether they have enough evidence to defend themselves, that’s up to them.)
Castro said Malacañang respects the Ombudsman’s action.
Asked whether Marcos was disappointed over Romualdez, Castro said she has yet to ask the President about his personal feelings regarding the matter. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Palace: SC may probe Sara Duterte's remarks vs. courts, police
articles.summary: Malacañang on Monday said the Supreme Court could investigate Vice President Sara Duterte"s recent remarks that she does not trust the Philippine courts and police.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 3:05pm
Malacañang on Monday said the Supreme Court could investigate Vice President Sara Duterte’s recent remarks that she does not trust the Philippine courts and police.

Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro was asked whether Duterte’s statements could constitute conduct unbecoming of a member of the Bar and potentially serve as a basis for disciplinary action or disbarment.

“Siguro po ang Supreme Court na po natin ang makakasagot niyan. Maaari naman po ang Supreme Court na magsagawa ng motu proprio or on its own initiative na pag-iimbestiga patungkol po dito,” she said at a press briefing.
(Maybe our Supreme Court can answer that. The Supreme Court can conduct a motu proprio, or on its own initiative, investigation into this.)
Castro was referring to remarks made by Duterte explaining why she hesitated to enter Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98 following the issuance of a warrant for her arrest.
Duterte repeatedly said she did not trust the police, the courts or even the security personnel assigned to protect her.
“I do not feel safe, I really do not feel safe. I don’t trust the court, I don’t trust the police,” she said in front of reporters and her lawyers.
Castro noted that the Supreme Court has previously initiated investigations into lawyers over inappropriate behavior or actions.

“Dahil nagawa naman po ito, itong motu proprio investigation sa ibang mga abogado na nagkaroon ng mga kakaibang mga behavior or mga nagawang mga aksyon na hindi masasabing tama para sa isang abogado,” Castro added.
(Because this has been done in the case of other lawyers who exhibited unusual behavior or took actions that could not be considered appropriate for a lawyer.)
Castro said Malacañang does not encourage Filipinos to lose faith in the country’s justice system.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Palace distances from Sara Duterte ‘special treatment’ at QC court
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday distanced itself from the alleged red-carpet treatment extended to Vice President Sara Duterte when she appeared before the Quezon City Hall of Justice over…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday distanced itself from the alleged red-carpet treatment extended to Vice President Sara Duterte when she appeared before the Quezon City Hall of Justice over the weekend.
Duterte arrived at the Quezon City Hall of Justice on Saturday to post bail following the issuance of an arrest warrant against her for three counts of grave threats.
The charges stemmed from her alleged threats against President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker Martin Romualdez.
Photos and videos showing a red carpet rolled out for Duterte as she entered the building, however, raised questions about why such treatment was given to an individual facing an arrest warrant.
When asked about this, Palace press officer Claire Castro cited the separation of powers between the executive and judiciary.
“Wala po tayong masasabi kung ano po ang naging dahilan ng korte [sa paglagay ng red carpet]. Iyan po ay hindi na po saklaw ng ehekutibo,” she said at a briefing.
(We cannot say what the court’s reason was for putting up the red carpet. That is no longer within the scope of the executive branch.)
“Kung ano po ang nais nilang isagawa na proseso sa kanilang korte, nasa kanila po iyon,” Castro continued.
(If they wish to carry out a particular process in their court, that is entirely up to them.)

Castro said there was nothing wrong with Duterte not having her mugshots taken, after House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon described the absence of mugshots as “special treatment.”
Duterte’s legal team submitted her recent photographs to the court in lieu of police mugshots.
According to Castro, however, an accused person is not required to have their mugshots taken exclusively at a police precinct.

“Sa parte po ng hindi pagkuha ng mugshot, mayroon po kasing proseso na kapag po kayo ay pumunta nang diretso sa korte at naglagak po ng cash bond, ang lahat po ng requirements na maaaring isumite katulad po ng mga larawan, sketch ng tahanan, kung saan iyong address, barangay certificate, at kapag ito naman po ay nakumpleto, hindi naman po niri-require na pumunta pa sa presinto para sa the usual na nakikita nating mugshot,” Castro explained.

(Regarding the part about not having a mugshot, there is a process where, if you go directly to the court and post a cash bond, you can submit all the required documents, such as photographs, a sketch of your residence showing the address, a barangay certificate, and other requirements. Once everything has been completed, you are not required to go to the police station for the usual mugshot that we typically see.)
Duterte posted bail for each of the three counts of grave threats filed against her before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court.
She appeared in person before QC RTC Branch 98, accompanied by her lawyers, Atty. Paul Lawrence Lim and Atty. Michael Poa, to post bail.
In total, Duterte posted a cash bond of P360,000, or P120,000 for each of the three counts against her. /gsg

articles.title: Duterte impeachment trial: Defense says CF payee names are ‘aliases’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — For the first time since the impeachment proceedings started in July, Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team stated that the names of those who signed acknowledgment…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — For the first time since the impeachment proceedings started in July, Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team stated that the names of those who signed acknowledgment receipts (AR) for confidential fund (CF) payments are “aliases.”
Defense counsel Justin Gular made the revelation during Duterte’s trial on Monday when asked by Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros to clarify the matter.

Over the years, lawmakers and lawyers have questioned the unusual names of those who signed the ARs for confidential expenditures made by Duterte’s offices — the Office of the Vice President and, previously, the Department of Education — such as the infamous Mary Grace Piattos.

“Your honor, given that this has become a material matter, we have to couch this answer that this is classified information, but these are in fact aliases … for the consideration of this court,” Gular said.
“But I hope you understand, your honor, that in threshing out this matter … we will do this at the appropriate time during our presentation of evidence,” he added.
Due to this, Gular said he would “veer away” from drawing conclusions of law and fact, as it is not yet the defense’s turn to present its evidence. /mcm
