articles.title: Confi fund recipients match names of children, dead people in PSA records
articles.summary: Some recipients of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education's (DepEd) confidential funds matched the names of deceased individuals and children in the records of the…
articles.byline: JOAHNA LEI CASILAO, GISELLE OMBAY, GMA News

blocks.text: Some recipients of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education's (DepEd) confidential funds matched the names of deceased individuals and children in the records of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), a witness in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial testified Monday.
PSA Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande said the youngest supposed signatory in the acknowledgment receipts was Marlin Sunga, who died in November 1965.
“Based po kasi sa death certificate po niya, two months pa lang ay namatay na po siya (because based on her death certificate, she died when she was two months old),” she said.
According to Grande, Sunga has been dead for around 57 years as of 2023.
Meanwhile, private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia presented the acknowledgment receipts of Fortunato Salig for P200,000, Emilio Sagan for P70,000, and Rodolfo Traya for P120,000, all dated 2023.

Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande said there are death certificates matching the names of Salig, Sagan, and Traya, dated June 2011, July 2015, and May 2021, respectively.
“Seven years nang namatay [si Sagan] noong 2022,” Grande said.
“Eleven years po noong 2022,” she added when asked how long Salig has been dead since 2022.
According to Grande, 34 signatories of the acknowledgment receipts have single-match entries with the PSA.
Meanwhile, Grande testified that there are 20 minors in the OVP’s list and five minors in the Department of Education’s (DepEd) list, based on their birth certificates.
Divinagracia presented the acknowledgment receipt of Miko Alquizar and Beatrice Cuenca for P400,000 each.
According to Grande, Alquizar and Cuenca were both born in 2022.
“Ilang taon na po siya noong 2022 (How old was he in 2022)?” Divinagracia asked.
Grande answered, “Isang taon po (1 year old).”
Divinagracia also presented the acknowledgment receipt of Mikay Delos Reyes for P200,000, dated 2023.
According to the witness, Delos Reyes was born in January 2020, making her three years old in 2023.
For his part, Senate Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero said that it is yet to be proven that the individuals who died are the same in the receipts.
This came after Grande testified that Traya died in 2021.

“Hindi ba dapat ang sinasabi mo mayroong Rodolfo Traya na namatay. Dahil hindi mo naman alam kung siya talaga ‘yun. Pero base sa talaan niyo, may ganoong pangalan na namatay, pinanganak o kinasal. Pero hindi ninyo alam kung siya din ‘yun o hindi,” he said.

(Shouldn’t what you’re saying be that there is a Rodolfo Traya who died? Because you don’t actually know if that was really him. But based on your records, there is someone with that name who died, was born, or got married. But you don’t know whether that was also him or not.)
Grande agreed and said that based on the death certificate, “may Rodolfo Traya na namatay (there is a Rodolfo Traya who died).”
Unusual
Meanwhile, Grande also admitted that she found the following names in the list of payees of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) as “unusual:”

items: Arthur Baon
Beverly Claire Pampano
Mathew N. Keso
Charles Sampaloc Jr.
Maxine Callos

blocks.text: “Ako po ay nag-verify some of the names listed, which I find unusual doon sa mga certifications,” Grande said.

Asked by private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia why she found the names unusual, Grande said because they were “unique.” She also said she conducted a reverification of the names using the Civil Registry System database.
When it comes to “Arthur Baon,” Grande said that, based on the CRS database, he has no copy of a birth, marriage, or death certificate
The same goes for Beverly Claire Pampano, Mathew N. Keso, Charles Sampaloc Jr., and Maxine Callos.

In the offering of the witness’ testimony, Divinagracia said that the prosecution is trying to prove that the confidential funds were liquidated “in the names of the non-existent, the long dead, and children.”

“Ang mga pangalang ito ang nasa recipient list at acknowledgement receipts ng OVP at DepEd sa 2022 at 2023—mga taong ayon sa talaan ng PSA ay walang record ng pag-iral, matagal nang patay, o mga bata noon,” she added.

(These are the names found on the recipient lists and acknowledgement receipts of the OVP and DepEd for 2022 and 2023—individuals who, according to PSA records, do not exist, have long been dead, or were children at the time.) —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Afternoon classes suspended in some Zambales towns, Olongapo
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Afternoon classes in all levels of public and private schools in several areas of this province and nearby Olongapo City were suspended on Monday amid continuous heavy rains.…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — Afternoon classes in all levels of public and private schools in several areas of this province and nearby Olongapo City were suspended on Monday amid continuous heavy rains.
According to local government announcements, face-to-face afternoon classes are suspended in the towns of Subic, Castillejos, San Antonio, Cabangan, Botolan, Iba and Palauig.
Schools in the municipalities of San Marcelino, San Narciso and San Felipe in Zambales and Olongapo City will shift to alternative learning protocols for the afternoon.
Schools in Olongapo City were advised to finish morning classes before allowing students to go home, while shifting to alternative learning methods for the afternoon.
The suspension was announced after the orange rainfall warning was raised at 11 a.m. Monday, indicating potentially heavy rains that could cause flooding and landslides in vulnerable areas.
Authorities urged schools and residents to continue monitoring weather conditions and follow advisories from local disaster response offices.
The move came as parts of Zambales continued to experience rainy conditions, with several areas still vulnerable to flooding following recent heavy rains./coa

articles.title: Tulfo: Use of CF aliases forgivable, but similar signatures questionable
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — While the use of aliases for the supposed payees of confidential funds (CF) could be forgivable, the signatures and handwriting on acknowledgment receipts (ARs) that appeared…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — While the use of aliases for the supposed payees of confidential funds (CF) could be forgivable, the signatures and handwriting on acknowledgment receipts (ARs) that appeared similar were “very questionable,” Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo said on Monday.

Tulfo’s statement came as the prosecution team in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial presented Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), its 11th witness for Article I of the Articles of Impeachment.

Grande’s testimony centered on the “unusual” or “unique” names of individuals who signed as payees on the ARs used by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) to liquidate their P612.5 million in confidential funds.

“Makakalusot pa sa akin ‘yun bang gagamit ng alias, kasi nga naman siyempre as an informant, especially giving intelligence information or confidential information, siguro allowed sila na gumamit ng alias to protect their identity para hindi sila masunog, ika nga,” Tulfo said in his manifestation during Monday’s trial,

(Using an alias can still get past me, because, of course, as an informant, especially when giving intelligence or confidential information, I suppose they’re allowed to use an alias to protect their identity so they don’t get exposed, so to speak.)

“Pero ‘yung bang pirma ng bawat, ng ilang mga informants po doon, pare-pareho, tapos ‘yung handwriting, ‘yung pagfi-fill up ng mga pangalan doon, pare-pareho, ibig sabihin iisang tao lang. So ‘yun ay very questionable for me,” he added.

(But the signatures of several of the informants there are all the same, and the handwriting used to fill out the names is also the same. That means it was just one person. So that is very questionable for me.)

Prior to this, Grande testified before the impeachment court that there were supposed payees whose names matched the PSA’s records, including a certain Miko Alquizar and Beatrice Cuenca who appeared to both be one year-old in 2023, the year indicated in the ARs.
Tulfo asked whether the prosecution team tried to trace the identities of the supposed payees, alleging that it was possible that their parents had signed the ARs.
Prosecution counsel Mae Divinagracia responded saying that they did not do so because they had limited time to track the whereabouts of the supposed payees.
Tulfo said that even the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the Philippine National Police (PNP) use aliases to protect their informants.
“In my humble opinion, aliases lang ‘tong mga ginamit nila, at ‘yung mga nagkakatugma-tugma sa mga birth certificate, ‘yun ay chamba lamang,” the senator-judge said.
(In my humble opinion, these are just aliases that they used, and the names that matched the birth certificates were merely a coincidence.)
Tulfo then reiterated that the signatures on the payees’ names such as ‘Pagong’ and ‘Pusa’ appeared the same.
“And I’m very sure, habang finifill-upan nila ‘yung mga pangalan na ‘yun, nagtatawanan ‘yun, ginagawa tayong mga kengkoy. ‘Yung mga tao diyan sa DepEd saka mga tao diyan sa OVP,” he went on.
(And I’m very sure that while they were filling out those names, they were laughing, making fools of us. These people here at DepEd and the people here at the OVP.)
Divinagracia then answered that if the names were indeed aliases, “the defense should have, at the earliest opportunity, already indicated that in their answer.”
She explained that because there was no mention of the names being aliases, they had the payees’ names validated with the PSA.

Defense counsel Justin Gular, meanwhile, responded that the Commission on Audit (COA)’s findings on the confidential funds did not include the names of the payees or the use of aliases as a point of concern.
“There was nothing to respond to,” Gular said.

“Your Honor, the fact remains at this point of the proceedings, and even at the time the articles of impeachment was filed, is that the prosecution had the burden of proof to explain and prove every allegation. If they are now claiming that these are aliases, the burden is with them, not with the defense,” he added.

Tulfo then said that it is important to call Col. Raymund Dante Lachica and Col. Dennis Nolasco, the supposed security officers of the OVP and DepEd, as witnesses to uncover the truth about the said names.
Lachica and Nolasco were the ones identified by the Special Disbursing Officers of the two agencies as the ones who “implemented” the confidential funds. /jpv

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines —The Philippine National Police (PNP) is planning to recruit 2,000 new police officers next year with a proposed budget of P700 million.

In a statement, PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. welcomed the proposed funding, saying the additional personnel would help the police force respond to emergencies, enforce the law and deter crime.
“The recruitment of more policemen means more manpower to secure streets and communities, enforce the law and quickly respond to emergencies and calls for assistance,” Nartatez said.
The Department of Budget and Management said the proposed funding would help improve the country’s population-to-police ratio and strengthen police presence in communities.
“If we can add more personnel, police visibility and crime deterrence will improve,” the PNP chief added.
The proposed recruitment is expected to help address the continuing need for adequate police coverage as the PNP continues its efforts to protect communities, prevent crimes and respond to incidents.
PNP officials appeared before the House of Representatives appropriations committee hearing on itsproposed budget last August 27. (Rendell Ivan Manuel, INQUIRER.net trainee) /gsg

articles.title: Survivor discovered in collapsed home amid flood devastation in Nepal
articles.summary: 'The four-storey house was swept (away) by the floods and the house was left in the middle of a quicksand. While walking around it, we heard a voice 'save me',' police officer Mahendra Darnal says

blocks.text: ALIVE. Chandika Kumari Shresth is found by rescuers in her collapsed home in Betrawati village, Nepal on September 5, 2026.
Screenshot from Reuters YouTube video
'The four-storey house was swept (away) by the floods and the house was left in the middle of a quicksand. While walking around it, we heard a voice 'save me',' police officer Mahendra Darnal says

items: Chandika Kumari Shrestha was found alive after her family believed she had died in the floods that devastated Betrawati, Nepal.
Rescue operations continue in the area, where hundreds are missing and many bodies have been recovered following the floods that killed over 1,300 people across Nepal.
Despite the grim situation, some survivors have been found, including an 8-year-old boy who was reunited with his mother.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
BETRAWATI, Nepal – Believing she had perished in Nepal’s deadly floods, the family of Chandika Kumari Shrestha started the ritual of mourning the elderly woman’s death.
Ten days later, rescuers found her alive inside her collapsed home in the devastated Betrawati village, where she had survived in a narrow pocket of air amid water and mud.
“The four-storey house was swept (away) by the floods and the house was left in the middle of a quicksand. While walking around it, we heard a voice ‘save me,'” police officer Mahendra Darnal said.
In a rescue operation on Saturday, September 5, lasting 45 minutes, Darnal and his team found Shrestha in a confined space and sent her to an army hospital.
“I was in touch with the family and they had started the 11-day mourning period,” Darnal said.

blocks.caption: Survivor discovered in collapsed home amid flood devastation in Nepal

blocks.text: Shrestha was among the hundreds missing in Betrawati, an area among the hardest hit by the floods in Nepal and engulfed with white deposits compacted almost like concrete. Crews continue to recover scores of dead bodies.

The town’s market and most residential buildings, some as tall as four storeys, were almost completely buried under debris left by a torrent that swept through the valley, part of a disaster that killed more than 1,300 people across Nepal. Thousands remain unaccounted for.

Rescue workers wearing hard hats were seen digging with shovels, while some were crawling through the gaps of collapsed buildings periodically blowing whistles to get the attention of anyone trapped and alive.
Five days earlier, 24 bodies were found in a decomposed state in Betrawati’s market area in a building that had contained a small shop, Darnal said.

blocks.caption: Family asks for help in searching for missing Filipino after Nepal flash flood

blocks.text: Eleven days since a glacial collapse triggered the devastating floods, close to 5,000 are still missing.

Hundreds of bodies have been swept onto the banks of rivers far from the ravaged Rasuwa district. In Chitwan, hundreds of miles away, several rounds of mass burials have taken place for unidentified and badly decomposed bodies.
Even as hope is beginning to fade, Nepal authorities continue their effort to look for people stuck in tunnels and under the thick deposits of mud that have hardened over buildings.
Since Friday, they have pulled out three people from the tunnels, including a Chinese citizen by the Trishuli river, where more than 900 are believed to be trapped.
Others like Shrestha have survived in extraordinary conditions, including an 8-year-old boy who was also reunited with his mother. – Rappler.com

articles.title: ‘Spare my kids’: Sara Duterte accuses gov’t of ‘child abuse’ due to surveillance operations
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte says the government's 'surveillance operations' on her endangers her family

blocks.text: VEEP. This file photo shows Vice President Sara Duterte.
Sara Duterte's Facebook page
Vice President Sara Duterte says the government's 'surveillance operations' on her endangers her family
MANILA, Philippines – Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, September 7, accused the Marcos government of “child abuse” because of law enforcers’ reported continued “surveillance” of her family.

Duterte made the statement two days after she posted bail for a grave threats case against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family, which was also the time she told the media that she feared for her life.

In her statement, Duterte said that since her security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) following the constitutional line of succession, she made “several important requests” to former AFP chief General Romero Brawner.
“Higit sa lahat, hiniling ko na igalang at protektahan ang aking ina at mga anak, at huwag silang idamay o takutin sa kahit anumang gagawin sa akin,” she said.
(Most of all, I asked that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they be spared or not threatened in any action that may be taken against me.)

She said that Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla and the police had “admitted” that they were aware of her whereabouts because of their surveillance activities, and accused the government of endangering her family, including her children, because of this.

“Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa lugar kung saan naroroon ang aking ina at mga anak, sa kabila ng pag-amin ng DILG Secretary at ng pulisya na alam nila kung nasaan ako dahil sa kanilang mga surveillance activities, ay isang seryosong usapin, lalo na kung nadadamay o naaapektuhan ang mga menor de edad. Ang mga bata ay hindi dapat ginagamit, tinatakot, o idinadamay sa panggigipit. Ito ay child abuse,” she said.

(Being in the vicinity or going to the place where my mother and children are, despite the admission of the DILG chief and the police that they know where I am because of their surveillance activities, is a serious matter, especially if the ones involved or affected are minors. Children should not be used, threatened, or get dragged for coercion. This is child abuse.)

“Mga kababayan, ang isang pamahalaang hindi gumagalang at nagpoprotekta sa mga kabataan ay nagpapakita ng kawalan ng malasakit sa kinabukasan ng ating bayan,” added Duterte, whose father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, had waged a drug war that killed thousands, including many innocent minors. (READ: ‘Far from collateral damage:’ Report shows 122 children killed in Duterte’s drug war)
(My countrymen, a government that does not respect or protect the youth shows a lack of compassion for the future of our country.)

In her statement, Duterte said she had known of an alleged “plan by Marcos” in relation to her as early as 2024, supposedly including the International Criminal Court warrant of arrest against her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, and the “attacks” against her.

2024 was the year Duterte resigned as education secretary, and effectively from the Cabinet, signaling her official breakup with Marcos. This was also the year that the House probed the alleged misuse of confidential funds by the Office of the Vice President and the Duterte-led Department of Education. – Rappler.com

articles.title: New videos of man in 9/11 lawsuit reveal extremist links
articles.summary: The footage and other evidence the FBI failed to share undermine Omar al-Bayoumi's 25 years of denials.

blocks.text: The man at the heart of a $1 trillion (£733bn) lawsuit brought by 9/11 families had extensive links to Saudi government officials and went paintballing with one of al-Qaeda's future leaders, video obtained by the BBC reveals.
The footage, which the FBI had within days of the 2001 attacks, stands in stark contrast to Omar al-Bayoumi's 25 years of denials that he was an extremist and a Saudi spy.

Bayoumi, who claimed to be a student when he was in the United States, is seen in one clip embracing Anwar al-Awlaki, who would go on to lead al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula. In another, Bayoumi and Awlaki are paintballing near San Diego with an official from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Islamic Affairs.
The videos form part of the 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia and have never been shown publicly before.

The lawsuit argues Saudi Arabia was complicit in the attacks and that Bayoumi aided two of the 19 hijackers who flew planes into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon - with another crashing in Pennsylvania.
Bayoumi was arrested in the UK by the Metropolitan Police days after the attacks and the videos were found among his possessions, along with other crucial evidence.
This included a diagram of a plane with a flight descent equation written alongside.

Multiple FBI agents received copies of the diagram, but it was never shared with the British interrogators, even though it had been couriered to the police station where Bayoumi was being held in custody.

The diagram was also kept from some FBI agents investigating Bayoumi, as well as from the 9/11 Commission - the independent inquiry into the largest mass murder in US history, in which nearly 3,000 people were killed. Bayoumi was never prosecuted.
He and the Saudi government did not respond to the BBC's requests for comment, but both have always denied any involvement in, or prior knowledge of, the attacks. The FBI declined to comment.

After a judge ruled the lawsuit could go ahead in 2018, thousands of documents, as well as videos and photographs, have been released to the court and also declassified through an executive order made by former President Joe Biden.

BBC Panorama and Radio 4 have examined these documents, and spoken to dozens of special agents and investigators, to trace the evidence the FBI gathered about Bayoumi and Saudi Arabia's alleged involvement in 9/11 - and to understand why it was never fully pursued over 25 years.
Our investigation also found:

items: The plane diagram was sent to the FBI's New York office and was analysed, according to an FBI source. But a US Department of Justice (DOJ) official told the BBC he was never shown a proposal to prosecute Bayoumi based on the evidence, even though "we've convicted people for less"
FBI agents in San Diego, where Bayoumi had lived in the US, repeatedly requested copies of evidence but never received most of it
The San Diego and Los Angeles FBI offices were both blocked from interviewing Bayoumi's Saudi government contacts

Staff on the 9/11 Commission objected to the conclusion that Bayoumi was "unlikely" to have been involved with extremists, prompting the report to attribute this to "our investigators who have dealt directly with him"

blocks.text: Omar al-Bayoumi arrived in San Diego from Saudi Arabia in 1994. He claimed to be studying English, but court records show that within a few years he had, in effect, abandoned his studies. He was more usually found organising religious events, often with a camcorder pressed to his eye.

One video Bayoumi filmed, from 1997 or early 1998, shows men, including Anwar al-Awlaki, paintballing. Filmed near San Diego, the group engages in urban combat scenes and target practice, many wearing military fatigues.

At one point, some of the men charge into battle, shouting "Allahu Akbar". A visiting Saudi sheikh is with the group and Bayoumi can also be heard addressing Anwar al-Awlaki with the honorific "Sheikh Anwar".

The following morning, in Birmingham, officers began the meticulous process of logging and bagging up evidence in his properties - a cache of many thousands of pages of documents, hundreds of photographs, flight ticket stubs, phone cards, and carrier bags and boxes containing at least 80 videotapes.

Within hours of the search starting, several items of documentary evidence - categorised as the highest priority at the direction of the FBI - were taken by police directly to Paddington Green, where the FBI had stationed an agent.

This evidence included a phone book containing more than two dozen names of Saudi government officials in the US and Saudi Arabia; flight simulator software; tickets and travel documents; and the yellow lined page of a notebook with the sketch of a plane, which an officer had marked: "contains handwritten notes mathematical calculations re height of planes".
Eighteen years later, the FBI would hand the notebook page to the court in the 9/11 families' lawsuit, following a subpoena. The page was made public in 2022.

"It's the mathematical calculation of the crash," Jodi Westbrook Flowers, a member of the 9/11 families' legal team, told the BBC. "When we figured out what it was, we knew that it was the smoking gun that we'd been looking for."

The equation, written in Omar al-Bayoumi's handwriting, indicates the height and distance required for a pilot to guide an aeroplane to a given object on the ground. Underneath it is a small drawing of a plane and a series of numbers.
Last year, the federal judge in the families' lawsuit found the notebook page, on the face of it, "connects Bayoumi with knowledge of the 9/11 Attacks".
In 2021, when questioned about it in court, Bayoumi said he had the diagram because he liked finding equations and could not remember when he had written it.

By the evening of 22 September 2001, copies of the plane diagram were in London in the hands of both the FBI and UK counter-terror police - and just metres from the custody suite where Omar al-Bayoumi was being questioned. Records show they passed through at least three further FBI agents in the following two days.

But here, the mystery begins. The FBI briefed the Met officers to question Bayoumi about the other high-priority exhibits, but the detectives in the custody suite were never given, or briefed about, the plane diagram.

Many FBI agents have told us the immediate aftermath of 9/11 was a round-the-clock frenzy. But it is hard to understand how a piece of evidence of this importance, in a case being handled with considerable urgency, was not put into the hands of the interviewing detectives.
The FBI declined to respond to our questions. The Metropolitan Police told us it could not comment because of the ongoing legal case.
On the day he would need to be charged or released, the Met detectives joined a conference call with several senior officials from the US Department of Justice and FBI.

Panorama and Radio 4 have spoken to two participants at the meeting. One recalls the British detectives setting out the evidence they believed met the threshold for the Americans to extradite Bayoumi to face charges in the US.
The response from the DOJ officials was that no extradition would be sought because there was insufficient evidence.
On 28 September 2001, Bayoumi was released.
But, at that point, the FBI had not shipped all of the evidence found in Birmingham back to the US, let alone exhaustively analysed it.
One memorandum from the FBI's legal attache in London, sent two weeks later, noted there were a "number of videos, floppy disks and documentation still to be viewed".
After Omar al-Bayoumi's release, agents continued analysing the evidence against him.
The BBC understands the plane diagram was couriered from London for analysis at the New York Field Office, which was in overall charge of the 9/11 investigation.

But we have not been able to trace any records of this analysis or its conclusions. A 2021 Presidential order required the FBI to declassify files relating to its 9/11 investigations, including into Bayoumi.

However, of the files released, the FBI has only produced one document referring to the diagram, despite its evidential significance, and this was only created 11 years after the diagram's initial discovery in 2001.
The diagram seems to have fallen into a black hole.
It was not passed on to San Diego, where Bayoumi had lived in the USA and where the FBI Field Office was also investigating him.

In fact, San Diego - where agents were interviewing his associates, searching his mosque, analysing his telephone records and bank statements - received almost none of the large volume of evidence seized by the Met Police in Birmingham.

Rick Lambert, who ran the FBI's investigation there, told the BBC his office made repeated requests to New York to send copies of all the evidence. "Their position was, we're in charge of the case; we'll send it to you when we're finished analysing."

Lambert said New York did not comply his office's requests. "I believe there is the potential that had we received that evidence and analysed it, that we would have been able to put the pieces of the puzzle together much more quickly."
Documents show that, in spring 2002, the San Diego office was ultimately able to get copies of a handful of videos by obtaining them not from New York, but from the FBI liaison in London.

Jeffrey Breinholt, then the deputy director of counter-terrorism at the Department of Justice who oversaw prosecutors working on terrorism charges after 9/11, told the BBC that Bayoumi's name had come up "as one of the hot possibilities for charges".

But he said the New York Attorney's Office never sent charges to him or his colleagues for approval. If they had, the plane diagram would have been significant evidence against Bayoumi, he said. "We've convicted people for less."
The paintballing video, Breinholt told us, is another "very telling bit of evidence" with the presence of Anwar al-Awlaki being "pretty damn significant".
"As a manager who reviewed a lot of proposed terrorism cases over the years, I can tell you that that would have jumped out. I think it would be a material support charge against Bayoumi."
There were no charges brought against Bayoumi.
Agents who tried to investigate Omar al-Bayoumi encountered other roadblocks.

In October 2001 in San Diego, Lambert and colleagues wanted to interview a number of Saudi officials in the US - many connected to the Ministry of Islamic Affairs - who they suspected had co-ordinated the help Bayoumi gave to two of the hijackers, Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar.
Because diplomats have a special protected status, the agents needed permission from FBI headquarters and the State Department.
"The answer came back, 'no, you're not going to do that'," Lambert, who is now a consultant for the 9/11 families in their lawsuit, told us.

Agents in Los Angeles experienced a similar outcome the following year, when they applied to interview a Saudi religious diplomat Bayoumi had met immediately after his first encounter with Hazmi and Mihdhar in the city.

"We hit a roadblock so hard, I think we all had airbag burns," said Steve Moore, who oversaw the FBI's 9/11 investigation in LA. Moore says his team made repeated requests to interview the official, but permission never came.
Like the FBI, the State Department declined to comment.

In October 2003, the 9/11 Commission - set up by Congress to provide a "full and complete" account of the attacks - interviewed Omar al-Bayoumi in Riyadh. He had returned to Saudi Arabia in the months after his release by British police.

The interview was conducted, in the presence of Saudi secret police, by the Commission's executive director Philip Zelikow, a former advisor to President George W Bush, along with a senior staffer and an agent from FBI headquarters.

The Commission's notes from the time record that Bayoumi was given a remarkable degree of reassurance during the interview. He "was told that no-one believes he knowingly helped the hijackers carry out their terrorist mission".

Bayoumi indignantly said he was a peace-lover who had become "a victim of the victims". During the interview, the delegation broke away for a multi-course dinner hosted by the Mabahith, the secret police, without Bayoumi.

After the interview concluded, the Mabahith told the American delegation they "would like to see him cleared". The Americans responded that no exoneration would be possible before their report was published.
When the 9/11 Commission Report was published in July 2004, Bayoumi was, in effect, cleared. It described him as "obliging and gregarious" and stated there was no evidence he had extremist views.
But some staff on the Commission were not convinced of Bayoumi's innocence, and thought it likely he knew Hazmi and Mihdhar were al Qaeda operatives.
The BBC can reveal that those staff objected to a line in the report concluding that he was "an unlikely candidate for clandestine involvement with Islamist extremists".
In the end, a compromise was agreed, and this conclusion was attributed to "our investigators who have dealt directly with him and studied his background".
The line was written based on the four and a half hours the Commission delegation had spent with Bayoumi, which included the interruption for dinner.
The Commission never saw the plane diagram, the paintballing video, written evidence of Bayoumi's alleged extremism, or much of the rest of the evidence the Met Police had seized.

Philip Zelikow did not answer the specific questions we asked him. He told the BBC the 9/11 Commission's findings had been subject to two government reviews, in 2015 and 2021, and the Commission had been "open about our suspicions and uncertainties. We were careful about whom to accuse of complicity in mass murder."
The Department of Justice told us it was unable to comment on matters and decisions from 25 years ago, involving staff who no longer worked there.
The head of the FBI's 9/11 investigation, Mary Galligan, has previously stated the Commission had "access to everything".

We tried to contact Omar al-Bayoumi through the Saudi government, but he did not respond. He has previously denied knowing Hazmi and Mihdhar were hijackers, that he was a Saudi spy, and that he had any involvement in 9/11.
The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia did not respond to our request for comment. It has previously said any allegation that Saudi Arabia or its officials are complicit in 9/11 is categorically false.

articles.title: 25 payees of OVP, DepEd confidential funds were minors – PSA
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Some recipients of the confidential funds disbursed by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) were notably minors, a statistician said on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Some recipients of the confidential funds disbursed by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) were notably minors, a statistician said on the 22nd day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Monday.

Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) assistant national statistician Marizza Grande, one of the prosecution’s witnesses against Duterte, noted there were single-match entries, suggesting several minors were among the recipients of the OVP and DepEd’s confidential funds.
A single-match entry refers to a single or isolated record or hit on one specific individual, while a multiple-match entry refers to several records, and a no-match entry.
“Based po doon sa verification namin, nakita namin na as per record, meron pong 20 na menor de edad doon po sa OVP list,” said Grande.
(Based on our verification, we found that, according to the records, there are 20 minors on the OVP list.)
“Doon naman po sa DepEd list, based on records po, meron pong limang menor de edad based sa kanilang mga birth certificates,” she added.
(Regarding the DepEd list, based on the records, five individuals are minors according to their birth certificates.)
Among the names used in the acknowledgement receipts cited by the prosecution were as follows:

items: Miko Alquizar – received P400,000 in confidential funds on March 28, 2023; born June 11, which makes him one year old at the time.
Beatrice Cuenca – received P400 in confidential funds on March 13, 2023; born Jan. 7, 2022, which makes her one year old at the time.
Mikay delos Reyes – received P200,000 in confidential funds on March 27, 2023; born Jan. 13, 2020, which makes her three years old at the time.

blocks.text: Asked who among the recorded minors was the youngest, Grande said someone whose records showed the person was only two months old—an individual named Marlin Sunga.
Oddly enough, the same records showed that Sunga was born in 1965 and died in the same year, on Nov. 2.
Grande, however, clarified that all this information was based on PSA records, adding that she could not categorically state that they were indeed the payees of the OVP and DepEd./coa

articles.title: Palace denies Sara Duterte’s claim on plan to ‘attack’ her
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday refuted statements made by Vice President Sara Duterte that she had received information back in 2024 regarding President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Monday refuted statements made by Vice President Sara Duterte that she had received information back in 2024 regarding President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s alleged plans to “attack” her and issue an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant against her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte.
At a briefing, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro denied Duterte’s statement, saying there was no evidence to prove it.
Castro also said there are no records that substantiate the vice president’s statement.

In a statement posted on her social media account earlier, Duterte said that since her security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in accordance with the constitutional line of succession, she deemed it necessary to convey certain important requests to former Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner.
“Higit sa lahat, hiniling ko na igalang at protektahan ang aking ina at mga anak, at huwag silang idamay o takutin sa kahit anumang gagawin sa akin,” the statement read.
(Above all, I asked that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they not be dragged into or intimidated by whatever might be done to me.)

“Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa lugar kung saan naroroon ang aking ina at mga anak, sa kabila ng pag-amin ng DILG Secretary at ng pulisya na alam nila kung nasaan ako dahil sa kanilang mga surveillance activities, ay isang seryosong usapin, lalo na kung nadadamay o naaapektuhan ang mga menor de edad. Ang mga bata ay hindi dapat ginagamit, tinatakot, o idinadamay sa panggigipit. Ito ay child abuse,” Duerte also said.

(Approaching or going to the location where my mother and children are—despite the admission by the DILG Secretary and the police that they knew my whereabouts through their surveillance activities—is a serious matter, especially when minors are implicated or affected. Children should not be used, intimidated, or dragged into harassment. This constitutes child abuse.)
Duterte said a government that does not respect and protect the youth demonstrates a lack of concern for the future of the country. /gsg

articles.title: WATCH: 398 of 677 DepEd confidential fund payees lack civil records
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Of the 677 alleged payees of the Department of Education’s (DepEd) confidential funds whose identities were verified by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), 398 were found…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Of the 677 alleged payees of the Department of Education’s (DepEd) confidential funds whose identities were verified by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), 398 were found to have no record of birth, marriage or death, Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande told the Senate impeachment court on Monday.

Grande said PSA received two requests from the House Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability to verify the existence of civil registry documents for alleged recipients of confidential funds from the DepEd and the Office of the Vice President (OVP).
The first request covered 677 alleged DepEd payees, while the second sought verification of civil registry documents for 1,992 alleged OVP payees. / dp

articles.title: House panel OKs total social media ban for children below 13
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A House of Representatives panel has approved a bill proposing a full social media ban for children below 13 years old, and restrictions on the technology’s use for those aged…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A House of Representatives panel has approved a bill proposing a full social media ban for children below 13 years old, and restrictions on the technology’s use for those aged 13 to 18 to shield young people from harmful content online.

During the hearing of the House committee on welfare of children, Pasig City Rep. Roman Romulo presented the still unnumbered substitute bill to 10 proposals seeking to protect minors from the dangers of unabated social media use.
According to Romulo, the full ban for children below 13 is meant to restrict them from having any screen time.

“Basically, the bill now will be a ban for all social media platforms for those under 13, and the reason for them is what we want is for them not to have screen time,” Romulo, chairperson of the House committee on basic education and culture and head of the technical working group (TWG) that crafted the substitute bill, said.
Meanwhile, restrictions for those aged 13 to 18 will include a ban on viewing short videos, messaging applications, and harmful content.

“For those 13 to below 18 years of age, we will have a ban on features, what features will be banned, first of all, harmful content which is defined in the law, these are topics revolving on violence, sexual, and similar topics,” Romulo explained.

“Scrolling shorts will be banned, and also chat groups will now be banned. So if you’re 13 below 18, you cannot join chat groups, you would have no other form of communication, so that is where we are headed,” he added.

Romulo admitted that the House’s version of the bill was different from what the Senate has passed. Senate Bill No. 2424 or the proposed Child Online Safety and Protection Act proposed that 16 be considered the minimum age for social media use
The bill was brought to the plenary on August 26, having been approved by the Senate committee on public information and mass media.
However, Romulo believes that such differences can be sorted out in a bicameral conference committee hearing, should both bills be approved by the respective chambers of Congress.

“I know that the version in the Senate is under 16, I am sure that every member here is more than willing, if this passes the plenary, to be open-minded and discuss with the senators in the bicam as to what we really want, but for now that is the version that we have,” he said.
Local office requirement

Romulo said another thing that the substitute bill also requires social media companies to “register a Philippine presence” if they want to operate in the country, so that they can be held accountable under Philippine laws.

“We’ve also required all platforms to register a Philippine presence. If you are to be accessed by any individual, corporation in the Philippines, you must be registered in the Philippines. And there’s a reason for that, is, kung wala tayong jurisdiction over that entity, parang very hollow ‘yong authority natin over the platforms,” he said.
“So we want them, if you can be accessed in the Philippines, you have to be registered in the Philippines,” he added.

Also, Romulo said the TWG purposely left out provisions related to limiting screen time, for adolescents, as they believe it is a matter that the whole House should decide during the plenary deliberations, specifically during the period of amendments.

“There are certain issues that is best to be, as I’ve told the TWG meetings, best to be discussed during the plenary, because there are certain situations that I think the plenary as a whole must decide upon, and that includes parental consent and also the limiting of time, if we want to enter into that,” he said.

“But I think that should not be decided by the TWG nor it should be constrained to the committee because all members should be heard, as this is an important piece of legislation on the direction that we want for this bill,” he added.

Suggestions for a social media ban for children came amid fears that unrestricted online access influenced students to initiate shooting incidents at the San Jose National High School in Tacloban City last June 22 and the Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City last August 18 to do these actions.
Three students were killed during the Tacloban shooting, while two, including the gunman, were confirmed dead after the incident at Ateneo de Zamboanga University.

There is a belief that the perpetrators in both incidents were supposedly exposed to violent content online or joined groups engaged in nihilistic violent extremist (NVE) behavior or senseless violence.
NVE is being looked at as an angle in the two school shooting incidents.

On August 28, Senator Risa Hontiveros relayed that Philippine authorities have been able to secure a commitment from Meta, which owns and manages social media sites Facebook, Instagram, and Threads, along with other messaging apps, to provide authorities important information should they spot a possible threat to children.

Before this, Malacañang said there is no immediate need to ban Facebook in the Philippines after the social media giant showed willingness to respond to government requests to remove fake news and violent content.

The possibility of restricting access to other social media platforms and other online gaming apps, however, remains should they fail to regulate content that could influence the youth to engage in violent behavior and the proliferation of misinformation and disinformation. /jpv

articles.title: How an IT engineer used AI to aid Nepal’s flood response
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — When devastating floods struck Nepal on the morning of August 26, Niraj Bhusal was getting ready for a routine day at the Ministry of Finance. When news arrived that the Rasuwagadhi…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — When devastating floods struck Nepal on the morning of August 26, Niraj Bhusal was getting ready for a routine day at the Ministry of Finance.

When news arrived that the Rasuwagadhi customs office on the China-Nepal border had been swept away, Bhusal, like many Nepalis, was dumbfounded. Unified, reliable information about the unfolding crisis was scarce. Bhusal knew he had to act, and quickly. That was when he decided to put his training in ‘AI and governance’ to test. Bhusal, who is an IT engineer at the ministry, worked through the night and single-handedly developed an integrated, accessible, and AI-driven disaster response portal to track casualties, locate missing persons and coordinate government relief.

Bhusal recently gained access to ‘Grok Bot’—the AI model developed by Elon Musk’s xAI. He has programmed the model to build the entire layout, design, and JavaScript coding for a web application called the ‘Rasuwa-Bhote Koshi Flood’ portal. Hosted on GitHub, the portal automatically aggregates and structures information from diverse official sources, including the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, Nepal Police, Nepali Army, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), news outlets, press releases, and satellite APIs.

To ensure absolute accuracy and credibility, Bhusal implemented a strict validation system. “Once the code went live on GitHub, the AI began sending new updates to my mobile phone every five minutes,” Bhusal told Kantipur recently. “To prevent errors, I verify each update manually. That first night, my laptop never went idle, and I only managed to sleep at 4:00 am.”

blocks.caption: Initially launched in Nepali, the portal is now also available in English to help Nepalis living abroad and international organisations monitor the situation.  Post Photo

blocks.text: As the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers raged, tearing through roads, power plants, bridges, and settlements, the AI worked tirelessly in the background, scanning the internet for news on casualties, relief fund commitments, missing person requests, ongoing rescues and official government statements.
Initially launched in Nepali, the portal is now also available in English to help Nepalis living abroad and international organisations monitor the situation.

What began as a simple Google Form to collect details about missing persons has now evolved into a critical node in Nepal’s disaster response architecture. After the government launched its official rescue portal, Bhusal integrated his database with the NDRRMA’s system, routing citizens who visit his site directly to official state relief and rescue portals.

To map physical destruction, Bhusal integrated satellite imaging from Copernicus, the European Union’s Earth observation programme, allowing the website to show precise damage to houses, roads, and bridges. Copernicus recognised his efforts, mentioning him on the social media platform X.

Bhusal’s solo initiative has sparked an outpouring of unexpected global support to keep the portal running. Shristi Mainali, a Nepali residing in Australia, contributed $210 in server credits. At the same time, Tabor T., a community developer at SpaceX AI (Grok’s parent company), stepped in with an additional $100 to ensure the site remained active during traffic spikes. Five other supporters contributed $185 via the ‘Buy Me a Coffee’ platform.

This is not Bhusal’s first time on the front lines of a national crisis. In his 13-year career in public service, he has served as an IT officer at the Ministry of Urban Development, the Prime Minister’s Office, and the Ministry of Water Supply. During the devastating 2015 earthquake, he was stationed at Tribhuvan International Airport and customs, managing the complex logistics of international relief materials.
Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle has highly praised Bhusal’s initiative, actively sharing and retweeting the portal’s updates on social media.
Bhusal now plans to officially hand over the portal to the government, hoping the state will adopt it as a permanent model for emergency communications.
Bhusal says that as citizens, everybody should contribute whatever and however they can in times of crisis.
“The government does not have to do everything alone,” he said. “I designed this portal treating every single victim as a member of my own family.” /dl

articles.title: Water levels at San Roque Dam, Pangasinan rivers remain under close watch
articles.summary: PANGASINAN---San Roque dam continued to release water Monday morning as several rivers in Pangasinan remained above normal levels, including one that remained above the critical level. As of 5 a.m.…

blocks.text: (Photo via Liezle Inigo)
PANGASINAN---San Roque dam continued to release water Monday morning as several rivers in Pangasinan remained above normal levels, including one that remained above the critical level.
As of 5 a.m. on Sept. 7, the dam’s water level was at 279.79 meters above sea level (masl), with an inflow of 338 cubic meters per second (cms) and a combined outflow of 746 cms.
Two gates were opened at the dam. Gate No. 2A was opened to 1.0 meter, while Gate No. 2B was opened to 1.5 meters. The Low Level Outlet was also releasing 125 cms.
The elevated discharge comes as authorities continue to monitor river conditions downstream, particularly communities located near waterways and flood-prone areas.

At 6 a.m., the Marusay River in Calasiao was above the critical level, while the Sinucalan River in Sta. Barbara, Pantal River in Dagupan City, and Agno/Bañaga River in Bugallon were above normal levels.
The Camiling River in Camiling, Tarlac was at normal level. No level reading was indicated in the monitoring report for the Bued/Cayanga River in San Fabian and Balingcaguing River in Mabini.
Residents near rivers and low-lying communities are urged to remain alert, monitor advisories, and follow evacuation or other safety directives when issued.

articles.title: Liberal operatives discussed whether to buy Porsche or Ferrari with developer’s payments, Icac hears
articles.summary: Rightwing NSW powerbrokers are alleged to have received illegal political donations from fugitive developer

blocks.text: Two Liberal operatives traded photos and messages about whether to buy a Porsche or a Ferrari with payments they received for Toplace projects they got approved via a New South Wales government fast-track development process.

The Independent Commission Against Corruption on Monday heard more evidence from lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood, a principal of Beckington Consulting, who is alleged to have shared in $2m in payments from the fugitive developer Jean Nassif, owner of the now collapsed Toplace.

Greenwood along with Charles Perrottet, a rightwing political powerbroker and brother of the former premier Dominic Perrottet, and Christian Ellis, a fellow conservative rightwing Liberal, are alleged to have received illegal political donations.

Dominic Perrottet is not a person of interest in Icac’s inquiry and is not accused of any wrongdoing. Charle Perrottet and Greenwood have denied taking illegal political donations. Ellis is overseas and is not expected to give evidence during the hearings.

Icac alleges that the payments were used to fund political outcomes, including the removal of the Hills Shire council and attempts to remove the building commissioner David Chandler, who had placed prohibition orders on Nassif’s developments due to defects.
The counsel assisting Peggy Dwyer has said the payments were split three ways between the trio.

Charles Perrottet and Greenwood attended a meeting in April 2020 with Nassif and around the same time Greenwood and Ellis had a text exchange in which they traded pictures of cars they desired. Greenwood sent a picture of a Porsche 911.
Ellis replied: “I don’t know. The top of the range one. It’s just insane.”
Greenwood: “There’s something about a red Ferrari always.”
Ellis: “That’s true too. That Ferrari is very nice, very very nice.”
Greenwood: “It costs about 280, same as that Porsche.”
Ellis: “Ferrari. Definitely.”
Dwyer asked: “You ultimately settle on a Porsche, is that right?”
“Yes, but not the $280,000 one,” Greenwood replied.
Dwyer said this exchange indicated that at the 24 April meeting between Nassif, Charles Perrottet and Greenwood was where huge payments for getting Nassif’s developments approved were discussed.
Greenwood agreed that the trio were offered $1m per project if they were accepted for the fast track.
The projects included 189 Macquarie Street in Parramatta, Garthowen in Castle Hill, O’Riordan Street in Mascot, a Cherrybrook project and perhaps one at either Clyde or Box Hill, he said
after newsletter promotion
The agreement was written on a scrap of pink paper that Nassif’s offsider Larissa Mouawad kept in her glasses case, he said.
Dwyer expressed surprise that Greenwood had agreed to this given it was potentially worth $5m to Beckington if all projects were approved. Greenwood said that was just how Nassif did business.

There were ultimately disagreements over paying for the Garthowen project, which involved a change to the Hills Shire local environment plan (LEP) and was a planning proposal approved in tranche three of the fast-track process, not a development approval (DA).
The DA for 189 Macquarie street, Parramatta project was approved in tranche five around August 2020.
The discussion to share one-third with Charles Perrottet occurred separately, Greenwood said.
At that meeting Greenwood said there were discussions about paying Charles’s payments to his wife, Anita, via her company Macquarie Consulting.
The $2m was in addition to the monthly retainer of $30,000 that Beckington had already agreed with Toplace.
Dwyer asked whether these payments from Nassif were also to be used to achieve political outcomes.
“And those political outcomes included the Hills council, didn’t they?” she asked.
“No, no, this money was just paying for delivery,” Greenwood replied.
Earlier she had taken Greenwood to texts where Greenwood and Ellis talked about getting Ellis’s mother into the deputy mayoralty.
The inquiry continues.

articles.title: 'Takot yan?': VP Duterte doesn't talk, act like someone who is in fear, says Adiong
articles.summary: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.…

blocks.text: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.

This, as Adiong chided Duterte for playing the victim card after being issued an arrest warrant for three counts of grave threats, which stemmed from claims of planning to assassinate President Marcos and other members of the First Family.
The Vice President’s ordeal prompted her to declare over the weekend, "I do not feel safe. Pakiramdam ko papatayin nila [pulis] ako (I feel the police is out to kill me).
"I have documented threats and harrassment since 2023. I fear for my children. I do not feel they are safe if I am with them," she also said.
But Adiong doesn't buy Duterte’s fearful facade one bit.
“Kung titignan niyo, hindi po ito yung taong takot (If you look at her, she does not appear to be someone who is afraid). Actually, in fact, it’s the other way around,” he said.

He also pointed to Duterte’s previous public statements that he said appeared to invoke violence against President Marcos, as well as her continued requests for travel clearance, as inconsistent with her claim that she had been under threat since 2023.

“Siya yung nagbibigay ng mga statement na nagpapahiwatig ng violence against the President, pupugutan ng ulo (She was the one making statements suggesting violence against the President, including that he would be beheaded)... So it’s not an indication of someone who’s been receiving threats,” he said.
These notwithstanding, Adiong stressed that any threat against Duterte should be taken seriously and properly investigated by authorities.
He said the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) had given her an opportunity to submit information about the threats she claimed to have received, but no such information had been provided.

“They were given the chance. They were called, invited by the NBI na isubmit po nila kung ano po yung threats na ... natatanggap nila (They were called and invited by the NBI to submit information about the threats they had received.
“Pero hanggang ngayon, wala po silang naibibigay (But until now, they have not provided anything)," Adiong noted.

Seemingly referring to Duterte’s subsequent criticisms on the court and police, the Mindanao congressman stressed that public officials should respect the courts and the law even when proceedings or their outcomes are unfavorable to them.

“In this case, whether or not favorable sa’yo, kailangan mo talaga as an elected official to prove to the people that we have our laws, we have to respect our laws, and only through our laws and through our courts can we defend ourselves."

(In this case, whether or not it is favorable to you, as an elected official you have to prove to the people that we have laws, that we have to respect them, and that only through our laws and courts can we defend ourselves.)
The law applies to everyone

For Adiong, the grave threats case demonstrates that the law applies equally to everyone regardless of status or position, rejecting claims from Duterte’s camp and supporters that the proceedings constitute political persecution.

“Ito pong nangyayari ngayon, ito po ang nagpapatunay na gumugulong po ang hustisya sa ating bansa. Wala pong tinitingnan na status or posisyon ng isang tao pagdating sa pananagutan at sa pag-implement ng mga patakaran o ating batas,” he said.

(What is happening now proves that justice is taking its course in our country. No one’s status or position is considered when it comes to accountability and the implementation of our rules and laws.)
He said the criminal case should also be distinguished from Duterte’s ongoing impeachment proceedings.
“Magkaiba naman po yung mga hukom na tumatayo dito at yung magiging verdict po ay magkaiba (The judges handling these cases are different, and the verdicts will also be different)."

articles.title: DSWD flags bogus UPLIFT aid for students
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood,…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) Assistance.

The posts claim that the government is giving ₱2,000 to elementary students, ₱3,000 to junior high school students, ₱5,000 to senior high school students, and ₱8,000 to college students under the program.
DSWD Assistant Secretary and spokesperson Irene Dumlao said educational assistance is not part of UPLIFT.

“Paalala po natin sa ating mga kababayan na walang educational assistance sa ilalim po ng ating UPLIFT Assistance. Ito pong assistance na ito ay tulong maibsan ang epekto ng pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin (We remind our fellow Filipinos that there is no educational assistance under UPLIFT Assistance. This assistance is intended to help ease the impact of rising prices of goods),” Dumlao said.
The posts also direct users to registration links, which the DSWD said are unauthorized.
Dumlao said there is no need to register for UPLIFT because its beneficiaries have already been identified using the latest Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) data.

“Mangyaring huwag po i-click ang inyong mga makikitang link na nagsasabing maaari kayong magparehistro dahil scam po ito (Please do not click on links claiming that you can register because these are scams),” she added.
Qualified beneficiaries under Groups 2 and 3 of the UPLIFT program receive ₱2,000 per month until December.

UPLIFT Assistance is among the Marcos administration’s initiatives to help poor, near-poor, and low-income Filipinos cope with the economic impact of the energy emergency brought about by the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East.
The public may verify information on UPLIFT Assistance and other DSWD programs through the Department’s official social media pages or the DSWD Online Grievance Portal.

articles.title: Alcantara, partner rule doubles tilt in Thailand
articles.summary: Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the ITF M15 Nonthaburi in Thailand over the weekend.

blocks.text: (Francis Casey Alcantara / Facebook / Impact )

Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the ITF M15 Nonthaburi in Thailand over the weekend.
Alcantara, 34, and Sornlaksup recovered from a second-set stumble and held their ground by protecting their 8-3 advantage to fend of their persistent Indian rivals.
“Thank you Pawit Sornlaksup for an incredible week and for carrying me through some tough matches!” Alcantara wrote on social media.
“It was a pleasure sharing the court with you bro! Special thanks to Coach Coach Carlo Core Tennis Academy BKK for always being there and helping me out again this week,” he added.
Prior to their title victory, Alcantara and Sornlaksup outlasted locals Thantub Suksumrarn and Tanapatt Nirundorn (7-5, 7-5) in the opening round.

They followed it up with a gritty 6-2, 4-6, 11-9 quarters victory over Japanese Shu Muto and Ko Suzuki to book their ticket to the semifinals, where they ultimately pulled off a 1-6, 6-4, 10-4 triumph against Americans Hugo Hashimoto and Michael Blando.
The tournament serves as a training ground for Alcantara, who will be competing in the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 late this month.

articles.title: Ely Buendia, Chito Miranda sell out Dubai concert amid Middle East tensions
articles.summary: Ongoing tensions across the Middle East have cast a shadow over the region’s live entertainment business, with uncertainty surrounding travel, consumer spending and large-scale public events making…

blocks.text: Ongoing tensions across the Middle East have cast a shadow over the region’s live entertainment business, with uncertainty surrounding travel, consumer spending and large-scale public events making concert planning a more complicated proposition.
And yet, some acts continue to defy the odds, demonstrating that music can be more than entertainment in uncertain times.
Ely Buendia and Chito Miranda were among those artists
The two brought OPM nostalgia to Dubai on Aug. 30, performing to a sold-out Coca-Cola Arena.
For the UAE’s Filipino community, the show also offered something beyond nostalgia: a chance to reconnect with home through live music at a time when the region remains unsettled.

Buendia, best known as the former frontman of Eraserheads, and Miranda, lead vocalist of Parokya ni Edgar, represent different eras of Philippine rock but share a deep connection with Filipino audiences.
The concert was presented by Tiana Entertainment Inc., headed by founder and CEO Bojie Yangco, who has worked in live entertainment for more than two decades.

The company has mounted Filipino concerts in markets including the U.S., Canada, Australia, the Middle East and Kazakhstan, with artists such as Rivermaya, SB19, Ben&Ben, Buendia and Miranda among its previous projects.

articles.summary: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the…

blocks.text: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the flood control scandal. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the Palace respects the Ombudsman’s decision as it is only performing its duties. “Iginagalang po natin ang aksyon ng Ombudsman dahil ito naman po ay nasa kanilang mandato (We respect the action of the Ombudsman because this is within its mandate),” she said. While the Palace had yet to receive a formal statement from President Marcos on the development, Castro said the President had already made clear his position on accountability. “Ang sa Pangulo naman po ay kung sino po ang dapat managot ay dapat na panagutin (The President’s position is that whoever should be held accountable should be held accountable),” she said. “Kung sino man po 'yan — kamag-anak, kaibigan, kaalyado, o kalaban sa pulitika (Whoever that may be — a relative, a friend, an ally, or a political opponent),” she added. Castro said the evidence should determine the course of the case, while those charged would have the opportunity to defend themselves. “Kung ano po ang isinisigaw ng ebidensya, dapat lamang po itong mailahad (Whatever the evidence shows, it should be brought to light),” she said. “Depende na po 'yan sa mga makakasuhan kung sila man po ay may sapat na ebidensya para ipaglaban ang kanilang sarili, nasa kanila na po 'yan (It will then be up to those charged, if they have sufficient evidence to defend themselves, to do so),” she added. Asked whether Marcos had expressed personal feelings about the case involving his cousin, Castro said she had not asked the President about it, but recalled his remarks during his fifth State of the Nation Address in July that he was prepared to let the evidence guide the government’s actions. “‘Pag ebidensya ang nagsusumigaw, kailangan po itong malaman ng taumbayan (When the evidence speaks, the people need to know about it),” she said. The Ombudsman filed the plunder case before the Sandiganbayan on Monday, accusing Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co of allegedly committing “concerted and coordinated acts” to unlawfully amass about P56 billion in ill-gotten wealth from 2022 to 2025. Romualdez has repeatedly denied involvement in the alleged flood control anomalies and has said he is ready to face the charges and prove his side, while his legal team has questioned the evidence against him. The filing follows Marcos’ July SONA disclosure that the Ombudsman was preparing criminal cases against his cousin. “Masakit man sa akin ito, pero kailangan nating gawin ang tama (Painful as this may be for me, but we have to do what is right),” the President said. “Hindi ako pangulo ng aking pamilya. Hindi ako pangulo ng aking kaibigan. Ako ay Pangulo ng Pilipinas at ang tungkulin ko ay sa inyo, ang aking mga kapwa Pilipino (I am not the president of my family. I am not the president of my friends. I am the President of the Philippines, and my duty is to you, my fellow Filipinos),” he added.

articles.title: Flooding hits 14 Iloilo City barangays; water up to 12 inches deep
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY — At least 14 barangays in five districts of Iloilo City were flooded Monday morning following rains that inundated streets and residential areas, with floodwaters reaching as high as 12…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY — At least 14 barangays in five districts of Iloilo City were flooded Monday morning following rains that inundated streets and residential areas, with floodwaters reaching as high as 12 inches in some communities.
The Iloilo City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) said that as of 11 a.m., flooding was recorded in barangays in Molo, La Paz, Mandurriao, City Proper and Lapuz.
The deepest flooding was reported in Barangay Don Esteban in Lapuz, where water at the Zone 7 Extension reached 10 to 12 inches.
In Barangay Taal, water was eight to nine inches deep in Zone 3, while about eight inches of flooding was reported near the Ising and health center areas of Barangay San Juan.

South San Jose recorded seven inches of floodwater in Zones 1, 3, and 5. Other portions of Cochero had two to three inches of water, while flooding along ICAG Road in Barangay Poblacion was one to two inches deep.

In Lapuz, aside from Don Esteban, water depths of three to five inches were recorded in Blocks 7, 8, and 11 of Barangay Sinikway. Flooding at the entrance to San Lorenzo Village in Barangay Loboc was reported at about six inches.
In Mandurriao, floodwater at Corner Block in Barangay Bolilao reached five inches.

City Proper also reported flooding in three barangays. Timawa Tanza and Villa Anita had three to four inches of water in affected zones, while Footway 1, Area 2 in Barangay Inday had one to two inches.
In La Paz, Barangay Divinagracia recorded one to three inches of floodwater in Zones 2, 3, and 4.

Photos provided by the CDRRMO showed rainwater covering roads in parts of the city, with motorcycles and other vehicles navigating flooded streets. Other images showed water spreading into residential areas as rains continued.
The operations center continued monitoring conditions across Iloilo City as of late Monday morning./coa

articles.title: Bereaved parents to give evidence at independent review of Sussex maternity services
articles.summary:
Review led by Donna Ockenden launches after campaign by families and media investigation into deaths

Susan Cacciacarro was almost 37 weeks pregnant with her daughter Chiara when she woke up…

blocks.text: Susan Cacciacarro was almost 37 weeks pregnant with her daughter Chiara when she woke up one morning in 2021, unable to feel her baby kicking.
“My belly just didn’t feel right,” she said. “I didn’t feel any movements.”

Chiara, her first child, had been diagnosed with a hole in her heart during a 20-week scan. Since then, Cacciacarro’s pregnancy had been classed as high risk and the growth of her baby had been regularly monitored in hospital.

But when a 34-week scan revealed Chiara had lost weight over the previous two weeks, maternity staff at Worthing hospital in Sussex did not make a plan to expedite her birth, which was planned to take place at 39 weeks.
On the day Cacciacarro woke up and realised Chiara was not moving, she rushed to the hospital, which is run by University hospitals Sussex NHS foundation trust.

Staff were unable to find the baby’s heartbeat and Chiara was delivered stillborn. “I’ve never felt so devastated and so crushed,” Cacciacarro said. “Your world turns upside down and suddenly it’s black.”

blocks.caption: Chiara in the arms of her mother, Susan  Cacciacarro.  Photograph: Susan  Cacciacarro

blocks.text: She is among the bereaved parents who will give evidence at a major independent review into maternity and neonatal services in Sussex, led by the senior midwife Donna Ockenden.

The review launched on Saturday with a public meeting in Brighton after months of campaigning by bereaved Sussex families. In February, a joint investigation between the New Statesman and the BBC revealed the deaths of at least 55 babies might have been avoidable if they and their mothers had received better care from University hospitals Sussex.

Ockenden, an expert on maternity safety, led the landmark review into maternity care at Shrewsbury and Telford and another into maternity services at Nottingham University hospitals NHS trust. She is also chairing a review into maternity and neonatal services at two Leeds hospitals.

At the meeting on Saturday, Ockenden discussed the review’s terms of reference with the families who will be most affected by it. “We need to get the finer details right to make sure that no family is left behind,” said Cacciacarro, who is now a mother of two. “I felt robbed when we lost Chiara … I’m hoping this review will provide answers to all harmed and bereaved families.”

As well as accountability and transparency, she said what was most important to the families was that the review brought about an improvement in the safety of maternity care services. “We definitely don’t want other families to go through this.”
When her appointment was announced, Ockenden said it was an honour to be asked to chair the review, which is expected to investigate more than 1,000 maternity and neonatal cases dating back to 2018.
after newsletter promotion

“I am absolutely aware of the responsibility I have to the families and babies across Sussex,” she said. “My priority will be to listen carefully to harmed and bereaved families and to engage comprehensively across communities and with staff ‘on the ground’ here in Sussex.

“We will proactively reach out to ensure that the voices of seldom-heard families are heard through this review. It is vital that the scope of the review now reflects the experiences of families and enables a thorough and meaningful examination of care, so that improvements can be made as the review progresses.”
The bereaved campaigners, who are members of the Truth for Our Babies group (TFOB), are urging other affected families to come forward and participate in the review.

Dr Andy Heeps, the chief executive of University hospitals Sussex, said: “Our thoughts remain first and foremost with the families whose babies have died or who have suffered harm when receiving care in our hospitals.

“We welcome Donna Ockenden’s review and remain committed to fully supporting the process so families can get the answers they need, and we take any possible opportunity to learn and improve. Our overriding priority is always to provide the safest possible care for mothers and babies – that is why our maternity teams have implemented many positive changes in recent years, and why we will work with the review team to find new ways of making our services better, and safer, still.”
A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: “Our thoughts and sympathy are with Susan [Cacciacarro] and all women and families who were failed by maternity services in Sussex.

“Through the national maternity and neonatal taskforce, increased investment in maternity safety, and the wider reforms following the previous Ockenden and Amos reviews, we are working to ensure families receive safer, more compassionate and more consistent care in every part of the NHS.”
