items: The Office of the Ombudsman has filed a plunder case against former House speaker Martin Romualdez over a flood control scam, making him one of the highest officials charged in this multi-billion anomaly.
Romualdez, who is related to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., is accused of being the 'central figure' in diverting public funds meant for flood control projects, which allegedly involved P56 billion.

In addition to the plunder case, Romualdez faces asset freezes and travel bans, with investigations revealing multimillion-peso properties linked to him, and the Ombudsman seeking testimony from former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan as a potential state witness.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Office the Ombudsman filed a plunder case against former House speaker Martin Romualdez over the flood control scam.

The Ombudsman charged Romualdez before the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan on Monday, September 7, making the former speaker one of the highest officials to be charged over the multi-billion flood control anomaly.

According to the Ombudsman, Romualdez, the cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., is the “central figure” in the alleged scheme involving “diversion of public funds meant for flood control projects.”
Earlier, the investigative body said the allegedly anomalous projects supposedly reached P56 billion.

The Leyte lawmaker denied masterminding the alleged kickback scheme, claiming that the national budget process is done not by the House speaker alone but by the entire House, the Senate, and the executive branch.
The Ombudsman filing was the latest blow against the once powerful speaker.

In April, the Court of Appeals ordered the freezing of assets linked to him after finding probable cause to believe they were connected to alleged plunder, graft, and direct and indirect bribery. He has also been placed under a preliminary hold departure order that month.
Romualdez asked the anti-graft court to lift his travel ban, but the Sandiganbayan denied the request.
The US government has also canceled Romualdez’s diplomatic and tourist/business visas.
As of April 22, Romualdez has already been barred from leaving the Philippines – the Sandiganbayan granted the Ombudsman’s precautionary hold departure order request against Marcos’ cousin.

blocks.caption: Leyte properties linked to Martin Romualdez: Tacloban Golf and Country Club

blocks.text: A Rappler investigation revealed there were multimillion-peso properties linked to Romualdez, including a P445-million mansion in Sotogrande, Spain. Another investigation also recently showed that the former speaker has ties to Tropics Hotel and to the Tacloban Golf and Country Club.
The Ombudsman’s latest ammunition against Romualdez is former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan, whom it sought to be a state witness.
It believes that Bonoan’s testimony can pin Romualdez and shed light on how lawmakers allegedly inserted allocations in the national budget through the Department of Public Works and Highways.

“We are requesting the Ombudsman to inform us if there is any allegation from Secretary Bonoan against former Speaker Romualdez and to give us ample time to comment on it,” Romualdez lawyer Ade Fajardo said.

“There is also the report that the Ombudsman has 28 new witnesses. We would like to know if there is any statement from them against our client, and we would like as well to have the opportunity to respond,” he added.– Rappler.com

articles.title: Ombudsman files plunder case vs Romualdez over flood-control scandal
articles.summary: Flood-control case against the former speaker reaches anti-graft court.

blocks.text: September 7, 2026 | 12:45pm
Then-Speaker Martin Romualdez (C) greets lawmakers after they voted to impeach Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte at the House of Representatives in Quezon City, Metro Manila on February 5, 2025.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa, file

MANILA, Philippines (Updated 1:00 p.m.) — The Office of the Ombudsman filed a plunder case Monday, September 7 against former House speaker Martin Romualdez and three others over their alleged involvement in the flood-control corruption scandal.

A copy of the Information also names former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, private individual Joselyn Traguia Serenio and Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Cristobal Guevarra as Romualdez's co-accused.

The filing came a few days after former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan was released from detention after the Sandiganbayan dropped him as an accused in a separate plunder and graft case. The Ombudsman had said it wanted Bonoan to testify as a state witness in other flood-control cases, including those involving Romualdez.
Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano arrived at the Sandiganbayan around noon on to file the Information for plunder under Republic Act 7080.
In July, the Ombudsman described Romualdez as an alleged "central figure" in a scheme to divert funds intended for flood-control projects.
Romualdez has denied wrongdoing.
Bonoan's prior release

Bonoan was released from the PNP General Hospital on September 4 after the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division excluded him from plunder and graft cases involving alleged P573 million in flood-control kickbacks.
The Ombudsman sought his exclusion after he agreed to cooperate with prosecutors and serve as a state witness. Bonoan still faces a separate bailable graft case before another Sandiganbayan division.
It was not immediately clear whether Bonoan's testimony formed part of the plunder charges filed against Romualdez on Monday.
Romualdez's camp had raised concerns over Bonoan's potential role even before the case was filed.

"We are requesting the Ombudsman to inform us if there is any allegation from Secretary Bonoan against former Speaker Romualdez and to give us ample time to comment on it," Romualdez's legal counsel and spokesperson Ade Fajardo said Sunday.
Fajardo said Romualdez should be given an opportunity to respond to any new allegations during the preliminary investigation stage. — with reports from Ian Laqui

articles.title: Former UK PM Cameron keynotes 27th World Knowledge Forum
articles.summary: SEOUL - Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron will lead the opening of the 27th World Knowledge Forum (WKF) today, Sept. 8, at the Jangchung Arena here under the theme "The…

blocks.text: SEOUL - Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron will lead the opening of the 27th World Knowledge Forum (WKF) today, Sept. 8, at the Jangchung Arena here under the theme "The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order."

Against the backdrop of profound discussions on the thoughtful coexistence of humanity and Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cameron, the 75th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, will deliver his keynote address on "A New Order of Co-intelligence in the Age of AI."
Cameron is expected to draw from his experience in reviving the British economy through deregulatory and structural reforms following the 2008 global financial crisis.
He will offer strategic insights on the leadership required to navigate today's compounding crises defined by the AI revolution and heightened geopolitical uncertainty.

Also joining the roster of speakers in this year’s iteration of the WKF are Go Negosyo founder and Association of Southeast Asian Nations-Business Advisory Council (ASEAN-BAC) Chairman Jose Ma. Concepcion III who will also receive the ASEAN Entrepreneurs Award together with Don Lam, CEO of VinaCapital.

Other speakers are Cho Jung-sik, Speaker of the National Assembly, former Prime Minister of Denmark Helle Thorning-Schmidt, former Japanese Prime Minister Ishiba Shigeru, and former New York City Mayor Eric Adams.
This year's forum will bring together close to 70,000 participants and 6,303 world-renowned speakers from 86 countries to share fresh insights for humanity as we enter the era of AI.

Dr. Chang Dae-whan, WKF founder and chairman of the Maekyung Media, said the 27th World Knowledge Forum is being held at a critical juncture, as the established order driving global economic growth collapses and protectionism and geopolitical tensions intensify.
“Confronting low growth and unexpected leadership changes, South Korea urgently requires comprehensive innovation and bold challenges across all sectors.”
“In particular, rapid technological advancements led by AI are reshaping industry and politics, throwing humanity into a sweeping transformation,” Chang said.

He added that while major powers invest astronomical sums in technologies like semiconductors, quantum computing, and robotics, concerns are mounting over winner-takes-all monopolies and job displacement, further intensifying social conflicts.
To break through these simultaneous crises, Chang said Maeil Business Newspaper chose this year's main theme: “The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order.”

“The mythical ‘Promethean Moment’ signifies a historical turning point when humanity received ' fire '—a revolutionary tool that drove civilization forward, yet acted as a double-edged sword if left uncontrolled,” he said.
“Likewise, we hope humanity can overcome this civilizational upheaval brought by AI with wisdom, ultimately architecting a new order where technology and humanity coexist,” Chang added.

Prominent speakers at previous WKFs have included state leaders such as George W. Bush, the 43rd President of the United States; Theresa May, the 76th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom; Nicolas Sarkozy, the 23rd President of the French Republic; and Gerhard Schrfder, the 7th Chancellor of Germany. Presidents of international organizations have also participated, including Jim Yong Kim, the 12th President of the World Bank. Founders and CEOs such as Bill Gates, Co-founder of Microsoft Corporation; Larry Ellison, Chairman and CEO of Oracle Corporation; John L. Hennessy, Chairman of Alphabet; and George Soros, Chairman of Soros Fund Management, have graced the forum. Scholars including Larry Summers, Paul Krugman, Michael Porter, and Gregory Mankiw have also addressed the forum.

articles.title: Jhonny Bobier breaks silence on ‘Tatsulok’ controversy, says he was ‘intentionally humiliated’
articles.summary: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he…

blocks.text: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he screened it publicly using fake MTRCB permit. In a video statement sent to GMA News Online, Bobier denied having anything to do with the alleged falsified Permit to Exhibit (PTE) linked to “Tatsulok Trilogy” and Tanajuan Pelikula Production. “I had nothing to do with that alleged fake MTRCB permit. I do not know where it came from,” Bobier said, as quoted by GMA News Online. The Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) earlier said “Tatsulok” had not undergone its review and classification process and had no valid PTE. The agency also said it discovered a fake permit connected to the film and its production company. Bobier, however, maintained that he never obtained an MTRCB permit for the film’s August 21 premiere. According to his account, this was his first time independently handling the requirements for a public film screening, after previously having such matters handled through film festivals. He said he relied on a Gateway Cineplex representative who handled the agreement for the screening and believed the cinema would inform him about the necessary requirements. Bobier also claimed he understood that a permit was needed for the planned August 29 public screening, not the August 21 premiere. The situation came to a head during the premiere when a cinema representative allegedly asked him for an MTRCB permit and warned that the screening could be stopped without one. Bobier said he decided to proceed with the event because the venue had already been paid for and guests were already waiting to watch the film. It was the timing of the issue that particularly troubled him. The director described the cinema management's decision to raise the permit concern at the last minute as suspicious, arguing that he should have been informed earlier if the document was a requirement. More importantly, Bobier said the incident left him feeling deliberately embarrassed in front of the people who had supported his film. “I cannot help but feel that they tried to humiliate me and embarrass me in front of those people who supported my film,” Bobier said. He further described the experience as being “intentionally cornered and humiliated,” saying it made him appear irresponsible for an administrative issue he claimed he did not create or know about. The filmmaker's comments come after Gateway Cineplex 18 issued a public notice on August 26 saying it was not associated with Tanajuan Pelikula or the planned August 29 screening of “Tatsulok.” The cinema also said the film would not be shown at any of its cinemas. Bobier said the notice prompted him to finally give his own account of what happened. He is now working with his lawyer and is seeking due process as the controversy continues.

articles.summary: The level of confidence seems very high, but can Alas Women Pilipinas translate it into success at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026? Can the Nationals match the historic fourth place finish of…

blocks.text: The level of confidence seems very high, but can Alas Women Pilipinas translate it into success at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026? Can the Nationals match the historic fourth place finish of the previous national team in the 1962 edition? It’s hard to make an early assessment considering what has transpired in the association over the past few months. But one thing is sure, Bella Belen and other Alas members are doing everything humanly possible to make their stint in the continental showpiece worth remembering. In a recent PVL On Tour gig in Victorias City, Negros Occidental, Belen, who plays for Capital1 Solar Energy, claimed they are trying to work on all facets of their game – especially on the defensive end – under the watchful eyes of Japanese coach Taka Minowa, to be at par with some of the region’s best. Belen is one 12 luminaries in a constellation of volleyball stars carrying the hopes of the entire nation, joining 452 other members of the Team Philippines in this quadrennial extravaganza. Actually, the Nationals need only to win once in their three-country group elims to advance to the quarters. While that sounds easy, it is still difficult since the 58th-ranked Alas has to hurdle the dangerous Kazakhstan before scaling the perilous Great Wall that is China. The Kazakhstanis are no pushovers being ranked No. 41, while the Chinese are rated highly at No. 7, second best in the region next to host and No. 6 Japan. The situation is even more complicated for the men’s side. The Alas Men landed in a ‘Group of Death’ alongside China, South Korea and Chinese Taipei and must beat two of these opposition to qualify to the quarters. Given more time to prepare this time around– it is scheduled to leave for Japan early to undergo training camp – Gilas Women is ready to rip up the charts and make a lasting impression. Joining Belen on the star-studded team are fellow Capital1 standout Erika Santos, former NU teammate Alyssa Solomon, La Salle’s Angel Canino, Marionne Alba, Dawn Catindig, Julia de Guzman, Thea Gagate, Ylizyeth Jazareno, Eya Laure, Dell Palomata, and Amie Provido.

articles.title: Government calamity spending surges 35% at end-August as disasters strike
articles.summary: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction…

blocks.text: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction requirements nationwide.

Data from the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) showed that cumulative end-August releases jumped by 35.3 percent from the end-July total of ₱10.4 billion. As of Aug. 31, the available balance of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (NDRRMF) stood at ₱26.1 billion.

This total is drawn from a ₱40.2 billion budget for fiscal year 2026—consisting of ₱23.5 billion for the NDRRM Program (NDRRMP), ₱15.3 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program (DRRAP) for local government units, and ₱1 billion for the People’s Survival Fund (PSF)—supplemented by ₱322.9 million in continuing appropriations from 2025.

To date, all disbursements have been sourced exclusively from the NDRRMP. The bulk, totaling ₱12.9 billion, was directed toward Quick Response Fund (QRF) augmentations for immediate relief and rehabilitation. Meanwhile, ₱1.1 billion was released for specific rehabilitation and logistics projects approved by the Office of the President (OP).
While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) was previously the sole recipient of QRF augmentations, several other national agencies have now received standby funds.

The DSWD remains the largest recipient, drawing ₱11.4 billion in total QRF replenishments across six tranches: ₱2 billion in February, ₱1.9 billion in March, ₱2 billion in April, ₱1.7 billion in June, ₱2 billion in July, and ₱1.8 billion in August.
Among other agencies receiving emergency funds, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) received ₱1.2 billion in August for its first QRF replenishment of the year.

The Department of National Defense (DND) received ₱300 million in July for the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) QRF, while the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) received ₱50 million in July for the Philippine National Police (PNP) QRF.

Apart from emergency relief, the ₱1.1 billion approved by the OP for targeted resilience projects includes ₱650 million for the DPWH to retrofit and strengthen the San Juanico Bridge in Region VIII, ₱385.1 million for the DND-OCD’s NDRRMC Integrated Logistics Hub at Lumbia Airport, and ₱44.8 million for DSWD command center repairs in Clark and rescue vehicle procurement.

Following these releases, the NDRRMP holds an available balance of ₱9.5 billion. When combined with the untouched DRRAP at ₱15.3 billion and the total PSF at ₱1.3 billion, the government retains ₱26.1 billion to address disaster-related and climate-mitigation requirements for the remaining four months of the year.

articles.title: Remulla: Sara Duterte camp sought 'drama' with handcuff, jail photos
articles.summary: Police say her security group asked where she could be held before bail was posted.

blocks.text: September 7, 2026 | 12:34pm

MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla claimed Vice President Sara Duterte's camp initially wanted her detained and photographed in handcuffs or behind bars after her arrest warrant was served, calling the proposed setup "drama."
"Ang drama nila, gusto nila nakakulong siya. Hindi kami pumayag," Remulla said at a briefing Monday, Sept. 7, at Camp Crame.
"Sanay kasi sila sa shortcut eh. Gusto niya may picture siya na naka-handcuffs, gusto niya may picture siya na nakakulong. Hindi namin ibinigay 'yon," he added.

(Their drama was that they wanted her detained. We did not agree. They're used to shortcuts. She wanted to have a picture of herself in handcuffs, she wanted to have a picture of herself behind bars. We did not give them that.)

Remulla made the allegation as the Department of the Interior and Local Government and Philippine National Police showed video footage to dispute Duterte's earlier claims that police harassed her during the service of the warrant.

"Any thoughts of harassment during the service are totally untrue. We dare them to present any CCTVs that they have in their office, in their residence of harassment that went on in the service of the warrant," Remulla said.
Asked about detention

Criminal Investigation and Detection Group Director Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico II said police initially coordinated with the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group because of Duterte's security arrangements as the country's second-highest official.
Morico said police offered to escort Duterte to the Quezon City court after booking procedures at the CIDG headquarters.
He said, however, that Duterte's security group informed authorities that she did not want to post bail and instead wanted to be detained.
"I was informed by the Vice Presidential Security Group that she does not want to post bail, she wants to be incarcerated. So they asked, kung saan ang jail facility," Morico said.
Morico said he told Duterte's camp that she would not be placed in a regular jail and could instead be accommodated in the CIDG conference room.
Authorities were later informed that Duterte would post bail.
She eventually posted P360,000 bail for three counts of grave threats.
Before entering the Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98, Duterte said she did not feel safe and cited alleged police harassment and surveillance.
Unarmed policewomen
Morico said he later sent a team to Duterte's residence in San Juan after learning that she would appear in court to post bail.
He said the officers deployed were all women and unarmed.
"No need for any other armed police unit because she has her own security detail coming from the Vice Presidential Security Group," Morico said.
Remulla said the footage showed no armed police component during the service of the warrant.
"As you can see in the service of the warrant, there was no SWAT, there was no armed component, the women were all unarmed. They were duly accepted into the residence and into the office," he said.

articles.title: Gabbi Garcia on Khalil Ramos' leading man era: 'Proud na proud ako'
articles.summary: As one of the most well-known celebrity couples of their generation, Gabbi Garcia and Khalil Ramos have kept it real both on and off camera. In an interview with the media during an endorsement…

blocks.text: Gabbi Garcia (Carissa Alcantara)
As one of the most well-known celebrity couples of their generation, Gabbi Garcia and Khalil Ramos have kept it real both on and off camera.
In an interview with the media during an endorsement launch, Gabbi shared how proud and happy she is about Khalil’s latest film, “Saving Cherry.”

“Of course, proud na proud ako. And si Khalil naman, I have no doubts about that guy. If other people tell me, like, ‘Uy, ang galing ni Khalil, ang bait niya. He is the best leading man,’ I have nothing but praise for him,” Gabbi said.
Admitting that she has yet to watch the film because of her busy schedule, Gabbi said she is nevertheless happy to see other people recognize Khalil’s talent and appreciate him as an actor.
For Gabbi, it is especially fulfilling to see Khalil receive the kind of praise she has long believed he deserves.
“Super proud ako sa kanya and walang question dun. I'm happy that I'm able to share him with other people kasi he really is a good guy,” Gabbi added.

Despite working on different projects and alongside both new and longtime co-stars, Gabbi and Khalil always find ways to support and complement each other. One example was when Khalil served as Gabbi’s personal photographer during the media conference for “The Voice Kids.”

“Actually, medyo nakakahiya yun kasi makikita siya ng mga tao na inuutusan ko siya. Wala siyang ayos that time kasi pack up na siya galing shoot, wala akong na-book na photog and need ko gumawa ng content,” she said.
According to Gabbi, Khalil even woke up at 8 a.m. just to accompany her to the press conference.
“Sabi ko sa kanya, sorry, bub, wala talaga ako na-book, so gumising talaga siya ng 8 a.m. para samahan ako,” Gabbi added.
After almost a decade together, Gabbi described their relationship as quiet but secure.
“Very supportive siya, and hindi kasi siya maingay na tao. Our love is not loud, it's quiet but secure,” she added.

At a congressional budget hearing, Angara said the consolidated funding for the joint delivery voucher program for senior high school students in the trade track and educational service contracting project for junior high school students faces a P3 billion cut.
“It’s reduced a bit, so that means [fewer] beneficiaries also,” he told lawmakers in mixed English and Filipino.
DepEd’s voucher programs aim to subsidize tuition for students enrolling in private schools, as part of its efforts to ease congestion in public classrooms.

In their exchange, Caloocan Rep. Edgar Erice urged Angara to ask President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. to redirect next year’s P58 billion local government support fund to education programs to cover funding shortfalls.
“Maybe Congress can also consider that because our youth are pitiful,” he said in Filipino. /jpv

articles.title: Stranded baby dugong in Antique gets help returning to sea
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY — Residents rescued a juvenile dugong that became stranded during low tide on Liwagao Island in Barangay Sibolo, Caluya town, Antique province, on Sunday. The dugong, or sea cow (Dugong…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY — Residents rescued a juvenile dugong that became stranded during low tide on Liwagao Island in Barangay Sibolo, Caluya town, Antique province, on Sunday.
The dugong, or sea cow (Dugong dugon), was found in shallow water during low tide. Concerned residents helped the dugong and eventually returned it to the sea.

Research showed that dugongs, once widely distributed across the Philippine archipelago, are now found in fragmented seagrass habitats, including areas in Palawan, Romblon, Guimaras, Negros, Fuga and Tawi-Tawi islands and parts of Mindanao.

Studies also estimated that the dugong’s distribution in the Philippines had declined by about 63 percent from its former range. It identified hunting, accidental capture or bycatch, dynamite fishing, and the destruction of seagrass habitats from coastal development and reclamation among the threats to the species.
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources has also acknowledged gaps in information about the country’s dugongs, including their population, distribution, and breeding areas.
While the dugong is classified as Critically Endangered under the Philippines’ national conservation assessment, its global classification is different.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) lists Dugong dugon as Vulnerable on its Red List of Threatened Species, meaning the species faces a high risk of extinction in the wild. Scientists note that populations across much of the dugong’s range are fragmented and the status of individual populations can be more precarious than the global classification suggests.
Dugongs depend primarily on seagrass meadows for food, making them closely tied to the condition of shallow coastal ecosystems.
Residents and visitors in Antique were reminded to avoid disturbing or approaching stranded dugongs and other marine wildlife and to report sightings to the proper authorities.
The juvenile dugong rescued in Caluya was successfully returned to the sea./coa

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment: PSA says no ‘Mary Grace Piattos’ in records
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Mary Grace Piattos, a supposed recipient of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential funds, has no records with the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Mary Grace Piattos, a supposed recipient of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential funds, has no records with the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), a statistician reiterated on Monday.
Based on the acknowledgement receipts submitted by the OVP to the Commission on Audit to justify its use of CFs, Piattos received P70,000 as payment of rewards.
During the impeachment proceedings, PSA Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande verified that Piattos has no records of birth, marriage or death.
“Based sa aming CRS database, wala pong nagngangalang Mary Grace Piattos sa amin pong record,” Grande confirmed.
(Based on our CRS [Civil Registry System] database, there is no one named Mary Grace Piattos in our records.)
Questions regarding Piattos’ identity first surfaced in 2024, when the House committee on good government and public accountability looked into Vice President Sara Duterte’s use of CFs.
“Piattos” is a famous snack in the country.
More payees lack records
Apart from Piattos’ identity, several CF payees from the OVP had no records under the PSA.
“Out of the 1,992 na listahan ng OVP list of payees, ay nakita natin na 1,287 ay walang record of birth, walang record of marriage o walang record of death na nasa database,” Grande testified.
(Out of the 1,992 OVP list of payees, we found that 1,287 had no record of birth, no record of marriage, or no record of death in the database.)
She added that 1,322 have no live birth certificates, 1,456 have no records of marriage, and 1,593 have no death certificates.
The same was observed for those supposedly paid from the Department of Education secret funds when Duterte was its secretary.
“Doon sa 677 listahan ng DepEd payees, out of the 677 po nakita namin na 398 po dito ay walang record ng kapanganakan, kasal o kamatayan,” Grande said.
(Out of the 677 DepEd payees list, out of the 677, we found that 398 of them had no birth, marriage or death records.)
Grande said that 405 of the 677 have no live birth certificates, 443 have no marriage certificates, while 507 have no death certificates. /jpv

articles.title: DOH starts early procurement of vaccines for 2027 immunization
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Early procurement of vaccines for the immunization program of the Department of Health (DOH) has been set for next year to avoid delays, Health Secretary Edwin Mercado said on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Early procurement of vaccines for the immunization program of the Department of Health (DOH) has been set for next year to avoid delays, Health Secretary Edwin Mercado said on Monday.

During the continuation of the House committee on appropriations’ briefing on the proposed budget of the DOH for 2027, Mercado told lawmakers that the agency has a proposed budget of P6.855 billion for its immunization program, including family planning and nutrition programs.
Parañaque City Rep. Brian Yamsuan asked Mercado if the agency has already proposed schedules for the immunization program next year to avoid the expiration of vaccines.

The secretary noted that some vaccines are delivered depending on their seasonality, such as flu and pneumonia vaccines, and the calendar of schools, such as human papillomavirus and cervical cancer vaccines for school girls.

“Latag na po yung schedule within the year. Doon po namin inaayon yung procurement schedule at ngayon ang directive ay early procurement na lalo sa mga mag-uumpisa pa lang ang taon ay kailangang ibigay na,” Mercado said.

(The schedule within the year has been laid out. This is where we base the procurement schedule and now, there is a directive for early procurement, especially for vaccines that we need to roll out at the start of the year.)
“Katulad nung influenza na by April dapat maipasok na yung order kasi doon lalabas yung strain for the year at dapat makapagprocure na para hindi maubusan,” Mercado added.
(Just like the influenza, by April, there should be an order to release [vaccines] because it’s when the strain starts for this year and we need to procure so we don’t run out of [vaccines].)
Mercado said the problems behind the procurement were in the process and not the financial aspect.
Asked by Yamsuan how the agency was going to address the gap in buying the right medicines, the secretary explained that the DOH must strengthen its inventory management system.
Mercado shared that the agency obtained technical assistance for its inventory system from the World Bank and the US government.

During the Senate committee on finance’s budget hearing on the DOH last Friday, Senator Raffy Tulfo questioned DOH officials about the expired medicines, citing photos of expired medicines allegedly buried by the agency.
Mercado then confirmed that P217 million worth of medicines expired in 2025. /jpv

articles.title: 37 alleged recipients of Sara Duterte’s secret funds are dead – PSA
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines— Government records showed that 37 alleged recipients of confidential funds released to Vice President Sara Duterte are already dead, an official of the Philippine Statistics…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines— Government records showed that 37 alleged recipients of confidential funds released to Vice President Sara Duterte are already dead, an official of the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) told the Senate impeachment court on Monday.

“Based po dito sa re-verification namin ng single-match entry, nakita po namin na doon sa mga pangalan under the OVP (Office of the Vice President) ay mayroon po mga talaan kung saan may records na po ng mga kamatayan o death certificates po at 32 po ay nakita namin na mga official death certficates samga pangalan na yun,” PSA Assistant National Statistician Marizza Grande said during the direct examination of private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia.

(Based on our re-verification of the single-match entries, we found that some of the names under the OVP (Office of the Vice President) had records indicating that the individuals were already deceased. We found official death certificates for 32 of the names.)
“Yung isang listahan po, pertaining po dun sa DepEd list, mayroon pong lima na official death certificate na nakita namin sa CRS (Civil Registry System) database,” Grande said.
(The other list, pertaining to the DepEd list, had five official death certificates that we found in the CRS (Civil Registry System) database.)
Duterte concurrently served as secretary of the Department Education (DepEd) from 2022 to 2024.
Divinagracia earlier noted that the OVP listed 1, 992 recipients of its P500 million in confidential funds while DepEd’s P112.5 million supposedly went to 677 recipients.
Duterte’s alleged misuse of confidential funds is one of four articles of impeachment lodged against her. /dl

articles.title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
articles.summary: JAKARTA — Jakarta’s main airport and three others extended their closure to 6:00 pm on Monday after being forced to halt operations due to a volcanic eruption, leaving tens of thousands…

blocks.text: JAKARTA — Jakarta’s main airport and three others extended their closure to 6:00 pm on Monday after being forced to halt operations due to a volcanic eruption, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded.
Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150 kilometers (90 miles) from Indonesia’s capital, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and plume of volcanic ash.

Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting hundreds of flights and leaving more than 170,000 passengers stranded, according to the transport ministry.

At least four airports, including Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, extended their closure from Monday morning to 6:00 pm (1100 GMT), airport operator Angkasa Pura said in a social media post.

“In connection with the increasing eruption activity of Mount Anak Krakatau, flight operations at several airports have been suspended; passengers are advised to regularly monitor their flight status with the respective airlines,” the operator said.
Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller airport that caters to both civil and military flights, also extended its closure, the company said.
The probability of an eruption remains high until Monday morning, the country’s geology agency said.

“The threat from an eruption comes from the ejection of incandescent rocks accompanied by heavy ashfall. Another potential hazard arises from lava flows if the eruption resumes and continues,” the agency said.
Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and left thousands displaced. /dl

articles.title: Butuan City declared under state of calamity due to water crisis
articles.summary: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425…

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425 families, or more than of its 269,000 residents, have been experiencing almost no-water service as water availability have continued to decline, particularly in the city's 11 most-populated barangays. Accordingly, the water shortage was linked to the prevailing dry spell in this capital city of Caraga region, which has experience a significant rainfall deficit. Butuan City Mayor Lawrence Lemuel “Law” H. Fortun ordered the implementation of water rationing in most affected areas, but these interventions have remainedinsufficient as the shortage continued. Fortun now centered the use of 30-percentQuick Response Fund to the most affected barangays. The state of calamity declaration is expected to allow the city government and affected barangays to mobilize additional resources and access Quick Response Funds for emergency measures, including the provision and installation of water tanks, tankers, pumps and filtration systems, as well as other equipment needed for water distribution and rationing. The state of calamity was declared over the weekend, during the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Third Special Session, the approval of SP Resolution No. 17-444-2026 at the City Hal Conference Room here. “The resolution was approved as the continuing water shortage has significantly affected residents’ access to water across several barangays,” the SP Resolution said. “We are doing our very best to address this problem,” Mayor Fortun said. The water crisis comes as Agusan del Norte and Butuan City, continues to experience a significant rainfall deficit. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) placed the province under “Dry Spell” status as of August 23, 2026.

articles.title: AI music, videos featuring Rene Baterbonia flood social media, streaming platforms
articles.summary: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning…

blocks.text: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning incident.
Among those circulating online are songs dedicated to Rene, with some using AI-generated music and others appearing to be AI covers or altered versions of existing songs.
One example is “Kalapastanganan,” credited to fitterkarma, which has been re-presented as AI covers of various genres and styles.
Other Rene-related releases include “Baon ang Pangarap,” credited to Andrei AI Music and “Tribute for Rene Baterbonia” by Nihvan.
There are also other music uploads carrying Rene’s name or referencing his death, showing how his story has continued to circulate beyond social media and into streaming services.
There are also AI-generated videos featuring Baterbonia in different scenarios, from still playing basketball to rising out of waters to begging for social media interactions.

These digitally created clips have added another form of online remembrance surrounding the late athlete, with his likeness being used to depict moments and activities that did not necessarily occur in real life.

The growing collection of AI-generated and AI-assisted content has effectively created a digital archive of sorts around Rene, combining original tribute material, covers, edited imagery and fabricated video scenes.
Meanwhile, Rene’s mother continues to ask supporters to keep the focus on prayer and the family’s ongoing pursuit of justice.
In a Facebook post on September 5, Rovelyn asked supporters not to hold a large celebration or bring material offerings to her son’s grave for his 90th or 100th day commemoration.
“Gusto ko lang ng simpleng pagdasal,” she wrote, explaining that she wants to prioritize the case involving her son.
Rovelyn also said that people who wish to help the family financially may send voluntary assistance directly to her instead of bringing food, decorations or other material gifts.

She included her e-wallet details in the post and asked donors to provide screenshots of their transactions for verification. The request follows previous statements from Rovelyn concerning financial assistance and the use of her son's name.
Rovelyn has consistently maintained that justice remains her primary concern.
“Hustisya po ang hiling ko di po PERA,” she previously said, while expressing gratitude to those who continued to support the family.
Meanwhile, Ateneo de Manila University said in August that it remained in communication with the Baterbonia family and was willing to meet with them to provide answers and support.

articles.title: Ombudsman files plunder charges vs Martin Romualdez over flood control projects
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman on Monday filed a P7.4-billion plunder charge against former speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez and three others over their alleged…

blocks.text: The Office of the Ombudsman on Monday filed a P7.4-billion plunder charge against former speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez and three others over their alleged involvement in a kickback scheme on flood control projects.

Aside from Romualdez, other respondents include former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, Joselyn Tragua Serenio who is the personal assistant of Romualdez, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.
Assistant Ombudsman filed the charges with the Sandiganbayan at noontime.
"Kaka-receive lang po ng Sandiganbayan ang kasong finile namin (The Sandiganbayan just received the case we filed)," Clavano said.
"It will be docketed. Up for raffle at 2 p.m.," he added.
The raffle will be conducted at 1:30 p.m. at the Sandiganbayan. No bail was recommended, as per judicial records of the Sandiganbayan, according to GMA News reporters Joseph Morong and Maki Pulido.
Romualdez's camp appealed on Sunday to the Office of the Ombudsman for fairness as it sought an opportunity to respond to any new allegations against him.

Atty. Ade Fajardo, legal counsel for Romualdez, made the appeal following reports that former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan may be pressured to link the former speaker to the flood control scandal.
“We are requesting the Ombudsman to inform us if there is any allegation from Secretary Bonoan against former Speaker Romualdez and to give us ample time to comment on it,” Fajardo said.

“Fair play and due process require that such information and opportunity be accorded to us at this point in the process, the preliminary investigation stage, not if and when the Ombudsman decides to file charges in court,” he added.
Romualdez’s legal counsel also requested information on the reported 28 new witnesses before the Ombudsman, including any statements they may have made against their client.

“There is also the report that the Ombudsman has 28 new witnesses. We would like to know if there is any statement from them against our client, and we would like as well to have the opportunity to respond,” he said.

The former speaker was first linked to allegedly anomalous projects in September 2025 when contractors Curlee and Sarah Discaya revealed the names of congressmen who allegedly demanded kickbacks, during a Senate blue ribbon committee hearing.
One of the congressmen mentioned by the Discayas was former Quezon City 4th District representative Marvin Rillo.
Curlee Discaya told the committee that Rillo mentioned Romualdez's name several times as his close friend.
Romualdez then branded the claim of Discaya as false, malicious, and nothing more than name-dropping. He said he would not allow lies to pass unchecked.
''Let me be clear: Wala akong kinalaman, wala akong pahintulot, at wala akong basbas sa mga ganyang gawain,'' he said in a statement.
(I have no role and I have not allowed this kind of action.)

''Congress debates and approves the budget. It does not release funds. It does not implement projects. That is the sole duty of the Executive and agencies like the DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways),'' he added.
Romualdez underscored then that he has never, and will never accept a bribe from anybody.
The former speaker was also mentioned as supposedly having used the Discaya couple as "front" to buy a high-end property in Makati City.
Romualdez however said he has never met the Discayas.

In September 2025, Orly Guteza, who identified himself as an ex-Marine and a former security consultant for then Ako Bicol party-list Representative Zaldy Co, claimed that he personally delivered luggage containing money to the residences of Co in Pasig City and Romualdez in McKinley, Makati City.
Romualdez however said Guteza's testimony was "an outright and complete fabrication".

In February 2026, a group of 18 men who identified themselves as former security personnel of Co — some of them former Marines — surfaced publicly and executed affidavits alleging that they had delivered suitcases of cash to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Romualdez, Co and other personalities. Four of them later recanted their statement.

Guteza also recanted his statement and executed a new affidavit, claiming that Senator Rodante Marcoleta and former House lawmaker Mike Defensor had tapped him to make up accusations against the Leyte congressman in exchange for money and scholarships for his children.

On July 20 this year, the Office of the Ombudsman announced that it is set to file preliminary investigation for plunder and the violation of Anti-Money Laundering Act complaints against Romualdez as a result of its fact-finding probe on his alleged involvement in the flood control anomalies.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla later said his office was very close to finishing its fact-finding investigation against Romualdez over the flood control controversy.

Despite the recantation of Guteza, the Office of the Ombudsman said last August that it still has 28 witnesses who have material information on the alleged links of the former speaker to the flood control mess.
Remulla also said Romualdez's camp was behind the recantation of four former bodyguards who also linked him to the flood control mess.
Romualdez's camp however maintained that there is no credible witness linking him to the flood control mess.
Fajardo said much of the prior 32 accusers of the former House leader have since recanted their allegations, including Guteza.
Romualdez's camp decried on September 1 that the Office of the Ombudsman seems to have "prejudged" him as the mastermind of the flood control mess even before the conclusion of its probe.
“Hindi namin maintindihan kung bakit ganu'n na lamang ang attention na binibigay nila, ang panggigipit nila kay Rep. Romualdez. Eh wala na namang credible na ebidensiya,” Fajado said.
(We don’t understand why the Ombudsman is giving that much attention to Rep. Romualdez when they do not have credible evidence.) —with a report from Llanesca T. Panti/KG, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte calls DILG visit to family home 'child abuse'
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday called the Department of the Interior and Local Government"s (DILG) visit to her children"s home an act of “child abuse” intended to instill fear, despite the…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday called the Department of the Interior and Local Government’s (DILG) visit to her children’s home an act of “child abuse” intended to instill fear, despite the agency knowing her whereabouts on the day the grave threats arrest warrant against her was issued.
Duterte previously expressed fears for her safety, citing police presence at the residence of her mother and children.
Following this, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla admitted that they already knew Duterte’s location on the night her arrest warrant was issued, but chose not to enforce it.
Duterte said Remulla’s statement seemed to be an admission of state surveillance activities against her, adding that children should not be dragged into “political harassment” aimed at her.

“Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa lugar kung saan naroroon ang aking ina at mga anak, sa kabila ng pag-amin ng DILG Secretary at ng pulisya na alam nila kung nasaan ako dahil sa kanilang mga surveillance activities, ay isang seryosong usapin,” Duterte said in a statement.

(Approaching or going to the place where my mother and children are—despite the DILG Secretary and the police admitting that they knew where I was through their surveillance activities—is a serious matter.)
“Lalo na kung nadadamay o naaapektuhan ang mga menor de edad. Ang mga bata ay hindi dapat ginagamit, tinatakot, o idinadamay sa panggigipit.Ito ay child abuse,” she added.
(Especially when minors are involved or affected. Children should not be used, intimidated, or dragged into harassment. This is child abuse.)
GMA News Online has reached out to Remulla for his comments but he has yet to reply as of posting time.
Request to ex-AFP chief Brawner
Duterte recalled a 2024 request to former Armed Forces of the Philippines chief General Romeo Brawner, asking authorities not to enforce any action wherever her children and mother are located.

“Dahil ang aking seguridad ay nakaugnay sa Hukbong Sandatahan ng Pilipinas alinsunod sa constitutional line of succession, minabuti kong ipaalam sa dating Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner ang ilang mahahalagang pakiusap,” Duterte said,

(Because my security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in accordance with the constitutional line of succession, I deemed it best to inform former Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner of a few important requests.)
“Higit sa lahat, hiniling ko na igalang at protektahan ang aking ina at mga anak, at huwag silang idamay o takutin sa kahit anumang gagawin sa akin,” she added.
(Above all, I requested that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they not be involved or intimidated in whatever action is taken against me.)
In her statement, Duterte attached a text message exchange between herself and Brawner.
Brawner assured Duterte not to worry, stating that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. would not allow anything to happen to her or to former President Rodrigo Duterte.
“If any action will be taken, it should be done outside your residence,” Brawner said in his message.
The Vice President replied that this was the most important point, as she did not want anything to happen in the presence of her mother and children.
“‘Yung important No. 2, huwag lang kung nasaan mga anak ko at nanay ko. Sabihan [lang] lahat hanapin ako sa labas,” Duterte answered.
(The important thing is item No. 2, just not wherever my children and mother are. Just tell everyone to look for me outside.)
Brawner responded, “Yes, Ma’am.”
Duterte appealed to the public, saying that a government that does not respect and protect the welfare of the youth shows a lack of compassion for the nation's future.

The DILG had previously answered the Vice President’s accusation of political harassment over tracking her whereabouts, stating that knowing Duterte’s location is neither “illegal” nor “unusual,” as it is part of the agency’s duty.

"She should blame the people around her. They informed us where she was when the warrant was issued. It’s our duty to do our best to know her location. That was not illegal nor unusual," Remulla told GMA News Online.
Duterte was issued an arrest warrant on Friday after a Quezon City court found probable cause to charge her with three counts of grave threats.

The charges stem from Duterte’s public statements in 2024 that she had hired an assassin to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez if an alleged plot to kill her succeeded.
Duterte surrendered on Saturday and posted a P360,000 bail that same day. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Enchong Dee embraces ‘yearner era’ with throwback photos of Erich Gonzales
articles.summary: Enchong Dee appears to have fully embraced his persona as “yearner.” The actor and TV host recently caught the attention of social media users after sharing a series of throwback photos with his…

blocks.text: Enchong Dee appears to have fully embraced his persona as “yearner.” The actor and TV host recently caught the attention of social media users after sharing a series of throwback photos with his former loveteam partner, Erich Gonzales over the weekend. “Ghost month pa rin?” Enchong wrote in the caption, accompanied by Ben&Ben’s “Lifetime (Reimagined).” The post quickly brought their former loveteam back into the spotlight, with fans revisiting the projects that made Enchong and Erich a popular tandem. The two first worked together in the 2009 ABS-CBN series “Katorse.” They later reunited in “I Do” in 2010 and “Once a Princess” in 2014. While their onscreen partnership ended years ago, Enchong has continued to occasionally revisit their old memories through social media. His latest post also fits into a running joke that the actor has seemingly embraced himself: his reputation as a professional “yearner.” Enchong has himself incorporated it into his social media persona through “Enchong Dee University,” a fictional institution built around his humorous posts and relationship-related “lessons.” The concept includes a tongue-in-cheek “yearning” program, with Enchong effectively presenting himself as a longtime student and/or professor of the art of longing. The running joke has allowed the actor to poke fun at his own social media habits, particularly posts that revisit old memories, relationships and emotional situations. His Erich posts have consequently become part of that larger online persona. However, while the “yearner” label is clearly something Enchong has learned to play along with, the actor has not publicly said that he wants to rekindle his relationship with Erich, who has been married for years now. Erich married businessman Mateo Lorenzo in 2022. She has also largely stayed away from mainstream showbiz following her last major television project, the ABS-CBN revenge drama series “La Vida Lena.” Enchong, meanwhile, remains active in entertainment, appearing in television and other projects while continuing to maintain a strong presence on social media.

articles.title: Breakneck finish looms as ICTSI Summit Point unfolds on Tuesday
articles.summary: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move. With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first…

blocks.text: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move.

With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first four legs producing three one-stroke finishes, another breakneck battle looms as the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets going Tuesday, Sept. 8, at the Summit Point Golf and Country Club here.

Quiban returns to the local circuit after a stint overseas, where he continued to sharpen his game following his stirring come-from-behind victory at Lakewood in the season’s opening leg. Que, meanwhile, is out to build on his clutch performance at Caliraya Springs, where he scrambled his way to a dramatic last-hole escape over fellow veteran Tony Lascuña.

And with Lloyd Go, winner of the last two legs at Pinewoods and Pradera Verde, opting to compete abroad in pursuit of added experience and game enhancement, the title chase has been thrown even wider open.
The stage is therefore set for another highly charged four-day shootout, with established stars, emerging talents and a growing band of contenders all capable of seizing the slightest opening.
Summit Point should provide the perfect test.

The course has held its own despite the recent mix of sun and rain, and while its well-maintained layout may look inviting, it can quickly turn daunting when approached without discipline. Softer fairways could encourage the Tour’s big hitters to attack more aggressively, but knowing when to unleash the power – and when to throttle back – could prove just as important.
The course rewards boldness, but it also exacts a price for even the slightest lapse in judgment.

Keanu Jahns leads the power-hitting charge, arriving with renewed confidence after a respectable finish in a rare Asian Development Tour event last month. The Fil-German, a four-time PGT leg winner who capped last season with the Match Play Championship, has been knocking on the door again and feels it is time to reclaim the spotlight.

Jahns opened the season with a third-place finish at Lakewood, followed it with sixth at Caliraya Springs, stumbled to joint 28th at Pinewoods, then bounced back with another third-place showing at Pradera Verde. He now hopes to turn that roller-coaster run into another victory at Summit Point.

Sean Ramos likewise enters the week with title aspirations. The young standout, who broke through for his first PGT victory in 2024, has spent the last two months competing overseas, further honing a game that increasingly looks ready for another championship run in the P2.5 million event organized by Pilipinas Golf Tournaments, Inc.
He is only one of a talented crop of young players determined to break through.

Carl Corpus has another PGT title firmly in his sights after claiming the Valley Golf leg last year. With the Asian Games looming later this month, Corpus is also using the event as an important competitive tune-up, seeking to find his rhythm early and build the form and confidence needed for the daunting Asiad challenge.

Aidric Chan brings a similar sense of purpose. The former national amateur standout has already secured his first professional victory on the ADT and is now chasing his maiden PGT triumph. Jeffren Lumbo and Russell Bautista are likewise expected to figure prominently in the mix.
But while the young guns bring hunger and momentum, Summit Point’s demanding conditions could tilt the balance toward experience.

That makes the presence of multi-titled campaigners Guido van der Valk, Rupert Zaragosa, Reymon Zaragosa, Jhonnel Ababa, Zanieboy Gialon, Michael Bibat, Jay Bayron and Lascuña all the more significant. Each knows how quickly a tournament can turn and, more importantly, when to press and when to protect a score.
The foreign contingent is equally determined to make its mark.

Korean Taewon Ha, who narrowly missed out at Lakewood, headlines the overseas challenge and returns with another opportunity to break through. Fellow Koreans Kim Tae Soo and Jisung Cheon, as well as Lee Song, are also in the hunt, alongside Japan’s Kashihara Hirotaka, Sena Shiraishi and Nagata Masaki.
With Go absent and no shortage of players carrying either momentum, unfinished business or a larger goal into the week, the Summit Point championship promises another wide-open affair.
The numbers already point to a tight battle. The course could make it even tighter.
And if the first four legs are any indication, expect the championship to be decided by the finest of margins.

articles.title: Contraceptives, including condom use, taught starting Grade 8 --DepEd
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) said Monday that the actual use of contraceptives is taught starting Grade 8, after Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña asked whether proper condom use is included in…

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 12:07pm

The Department of Education (DepEd) said Monday that the actual use of contraceptives is taught starting Grade 8, after Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña asked whether proper condom use is included in reproductive health education for students.

Cendaña raised the issue during the House committee on apppropriations’ hearing on DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget, citing the country’s concerns over adolescent pregnancy and HIV as well as recent cases of school violence.

“Nabanggit ko po kanina na pabata nang pabata ang nakakaroon ng HIV sa ating bansa, at alam n’yo naman po kung gaano katiyaga ang ating passionate advocating for reproductive health education. At 'yung isa pong tanong na palagi naming tinatanong sa DepEd ay given the situation, ituturo na po ba natin ang proper condom use sa ating mga estudyante, at ituturo po sa anong edad po ito ituturo?” he asked.

(I mentioned earlier that HIV patients are getting younger and younger, and you know how passionate I have been in advocating for reproductive health education. And one question we always ask DepEd is, given the situation, will we now teach proper condom use to our students, and at what age will this be taught?)
Education Secretary Sonny Angara said responsible reproductive health and ways to avoid unwanted pregnancies are part of the curriculum.

“Definitely, that’s a requirement of the reproductive health law, Your Honor. So I just have to check what age it’s being taught with our curriculum personnel. But definitely, ways to avoid unwanted pregnancies, responsible reproductive health, these are all parts of our curriculum and things we need to impart to our young people,” he answered.
Angara then specified that the actual use of contraceptives is taught in Grade 8.

“So I think pagdating po sa body parts, that’s taught very early, I think stage one or stage two. But the actual use of contraceptives is taught at eighth grade, Your Honor. Eighth grade po,” he added.
(So I think when it comes to body parts, that’s taught very early, I think stage one or stage two. But the actual use of contraceptives is taught at eighth grade, Your Honor. Eighth grade.)
DepEd to submit curriculum standards
Cendaña said he had been involved in developing the curriculum standards for comprehensive sexuality education and asked DepEd to provide the standards that would be used for the rollout.
He said the committee would take note of Angara’s commitment regarding the teaching of proper condom use and protection in Grade 8.

“So again, we will take your commitment na ituturo ang proper use of condom and protection sa ating eighth grade. And we request the DepEd to submit to this committee the curriculum standards that will be used for this particular rollout.”

(So again, we will take your commitment that the proper use of condoms and protection will be taught in Grade 8. And we request the DepEd to submit to this committee the curriculum standards that will be used for this particular rollout.)
Angara agreed to provide the curriculum standards.
“We’ll do so, Madam Chair, Your Honor,” he said. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Europe wrestles with impact of historic regional gains for Germany's AfD
articles.summary: The BBC's Europe editor Katya Adler sees the far-right win in Saxony-Anhalt state ringing alarm bells for the EU and traditional parties.

blocks.text: "Seismic", "a socio-political earthquake", "a watershed moment for Germany".

This was how political analysts and many media outlets described the stunning victory of the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in local elections in Germany on Sunday. Is that an exaggeration?

Saxony-Anhalt is one of the smallest of massive Germany's 16 regions. It boasts a mere 1.7m out of 59m eligible voters nationwide. How significant can its political sentiments be, especially since the AfD narrowly failed to win an outright majority?
The answer: very significant.
First and foremost, at home in Germany.

The vote may have been regional but it impacts at national level. The AfD landslide piles even more pressure on the already beleaguered centrist coalition government in Berlin. It may prove to be the nail in the political coffin of Germany's deeply unpopular conservative Chancellor, Friedrich Merz. He had promised to slash the AfD's popularity.

These political woes will further weaken and distract Germany, the EU's most powerful player, at a time of continental crisis - as Europe struggles to contain Russian aggression, Donald Trump's tariff tantrums and the economic threat from China.

The Saxony-Anhalt result also provokes soul-searching throughout Germany, where the Nazi past still looms large. This is the first outstanding electoral landslide for a hard right nationalist party since the fall of the Third Reich in 1945.
The German authorities have labelled the AfD, in part, anti-democratic and a number of regional factions of the party, including Saxony-Anhalt, far right extremist.
The AfD is well known to be particularly popular in east Germany but it's now also polling as the biggest political party nationwide.
Germany's political mainstream has failed voters, it would seem. What does Europe's biggest single economy, its most populous nation not counting Russia, do now?
Tiny Saxony-Anhalt is causing waves outside Germany too.
None other than the President of the United States swiftly posted the Saxony-Anhalt exit poll on his Truth Social platform on Sunday.

The AfD's anti-immigration, anti-woke, "Germany for Germans" message chimes closely with Donald Trump's MAGA missive. Along with a number of other nationalist parties in Europe, the AfD borrows heavily from the Trump playbook - undermining mainstream media, questioning the neutrality of judges and promising to "make Germany great again".
Interesting to note though - the US president is rarely name-checked on the campaign trail in Europe. Politicians are keenly aware just how unpopular he is amongst voters.

Hot on Donald Trump's social media heels on Sunday night was the influential Russian businessman Kirill Dmitriev, CEO of the Russian Direct Investment Fund. He declared the AfD result "historic", Germany's national government "discredited" and the German Chancellor "humiliated", comparing Friedrich Merz to the UK's not-long-gone prime minister, Keir Starmer, who felt forced to resign this summer.
What interest might Russia have in German regional elections, you might ask, and what was Dmitriev's dig at the UK all about?
The German government is the largest single donor to Ukraine and the UK is known to have provided Kyiv with missiles used to strike inside Russian territory. This has deeply angered Moscow.

The AfD, by comparison, is pretty pro-Russia. It wants to stop sending military aid to Ukraine, halt sanctions against Moscow and start buying much cheaper Russian energy again. Energy-hungry German industry suffered a huge economic blow after the country halted Russian energy imports, following the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The AfD's softly-softly approach to Russia has another appeal in Germany's east, which remains far poorer than the west. This, despite Germany spending between 2.3 and 3 trillion euros (depending on reports and whether inflation is taken into account) to help integrate the former communist part of the country after the 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall.

Saxony-Anhalt is Germany's poorest region and there, as in much of east Germany, you often encounter what's known as "Ostalgie" amongst voters; essentially "nostalgia in the east" for comparatively more stable times under communism.

Also watching the Saxony-Anhalt election closely was the European Union. The next 12 months is bumper election season across the EU. Ballots are expected in key nations France, Italy, Spain and Poland. Brussels fears more "extreme" parties, left but particularly right of the political spectrum, may benefit across the board.
The leader of Spain's nationalist Vox party, Santiago Abascal, posted on X on Sunday that the AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt was " a great hope for Germany and for Europe".

By contrast, France's Europe Minister, Benjamin Haddad, an ally of centrist President Emmanuel Macron, warned "this is a serious moment in Europe, seeing the far right win in a regional election in Germany".

Neither the AfD, nor other European parties labelled "extreme right" or "hard right", accept the label. They also differ from one another in tone and party programme. France's National Rally under Marine Le Pen kicked the AfD out of its grouping in the European Parliament two years ago, for being too "radical". What the parties do tend to share, however, is an anti-immigration platform and strong nationalist messaging. And that really worries the EU.

Whether it's a rallying cry for "Germany First" or "Italy First" or "France for the French!", the concern in Brussels is that the rise of nationalist parties strains European cohesion at a time when outside events demand it more than ever.

Nationalist parties like the AfD or Italy's League Party tend to be deeply Eurosceptic, but Brussels says Europe needs to stand united to counter Donald Trump's bullying, for example, or to effectively protect European business against China's goods dumping.

Europe's defence establishment also warns that fractures in European sanctions against Russia or countries going tepid on Nato membership (as you see in Marine Le Pen's National Rally for example, or Germany's AfD) just emboldens Moscow.
Security chiefs say nations must stick together to stop Russia in Ukraine, otherwise the Kremlin will be tempted to attack inside Nato, such as the Baltic states.

The thing is, Europe's voters are very aware of these outside threats and the impact they have at home. They worry about the impact of wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, about crumbling health services at home and dwindling economic security for themselves and their family. Uncontrolled immigration and safety on the streets are huge concerns too.

And this is where the significance of the Saxony-Anhalt vote shines bright. A flashing red warning to traditional political parties, but also to institutions across Europe like the judiciary and security services. Those the AfD dismisses as the self-interested "Establishment".

Voters on this continent feel lost and let down by parties they've supported over and again for decades. Looking right or left now at election time does not mean they've all suddenly become extremist.

The AfD campaign slogan in Saxony-Anhalt was an upbeat "Anything is Possible!" Plus a promise to make Germans feel proud of their country again. Till now untried and untested in government, people seem increasingly willing to give them a go.
